ORDER SHEET
IN THE ISLAMABAD HIGH COURT, ISLAMABAD.
JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT.
Crl. Misc. No.1956-B-2025
Fahad
Versus
The State and another.
S. No. of Date of Order with signature of Judge and that of parties or
order/ order/ counsel where necessary.
proceedings Proceedings
(04) 24.11.2025 Mr. Talha Sarfraz, Advocate through Video Link.
Mr. Usman Rasool Ghumman, AAG.
Mr. Shahid Shabbir, Advocate for the complainant.
Asif Nawaz, D.D CCRC, ICT.
Asim Shahjehan, Inspector, CCRC, Islamabad.
MOHSIN AKHTAR KAYANI J. Through the
instant petition, the petitioner has prayed for the
grant of post-arrest bail in criminal case F.I.R
No.40/23 dated 09.02.2023 registered under Section
11 of PECA, 2016 read with Sections 295-A, 295-B,
295-C, 298-A, 109 PPC at P.S. FIA, Cybercrime
Circle, Islamabad.
2. Brief facts referred in the instant FIR lodged on
the complaint of Respondent No.2, Aamir Zafar, are
as follows:
“Consequent upon conclusion of enquiry No. RE-
171/2023 of FIA Cyber Crime Reporting Center,
Islamabad, it transpired that the accused Raja
Muhammad Adil s/o Raja Muhammad Banaras r/o
Pind Malhu. Tehsil and District Rawalpindi. CNIC
42501-7586051-5. User of Facebook Profile having
URL https://www.facebook.com/
profile.php?id=100085713667317 Profile name:
'Salman Ahmad with criminal intentions & ulterior
motives, illegally and unauthorizedly, created /
developed and further uploaded/transmitted/
disseminated as well as publicly projected /
displayed blasphemous contents i.e., Images /
Pictures, in respect of The Almighty The Holy
Prophet and
2
Crl. Misc. No.1956-B-2025
The Holy The Holy ﯽﻠﺻ
along with sacrilegious, loathsome
narration/speech, and text on private parts of the
necked human body using Facebook Profile having
URL https://www.facebook.com/
profile.php?id=10008-5713667317 Profile name:
'Salman Ahmad participating with/in different
Facebook Profile/s and / Group/s and willfully
defiled and outraged Religious Feelings. Belief as
well as Spirit of Islam. Furthermore, during the
course of enquiry in the subject case, Mobile Phone
Set Huawei IMEI 1: 869783043770347 and IMEI 2:
869783043810358, along with mobile phone sims
0332-2120487, 0317-5117176 as well as Facebook
Profile having URL:
https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=1000857
-13667317 Profile name: 'Salman Ahmad being used
in the commission of subject offences, were recovered
from the aforementioned accused Raja Muhammad
Adil.”
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner contends
that the petitioner is innocent and has falsely been
implicated in this case; that the petitioner is a
student of MSc Agriculture in the University and has
no relationship or nexus with the crime; that
petitioner first post arrest bail petition was
dismissed on 22.05.2023 and presently he served 02
years and 07 months behind the bars. However, from
the date of his arrest, he spent 02 years and 08
months behind the bars, but his trial has not yet
been concluded; that his co-accused Raja
Muhammad Adil was the principal accused, who was
granted post arrest bail by this Court vide order
dated 02.10.2025, passed in Crl. Misc. No.1468-B-
2025 and as such principle of consistency is
applicable in this case.
4. Conversely, learned AAG as well as learned
counsel for the complainant has opposed the instant
3
Crl. Misc. No.1956-B-2025
post arrest bail on the ground that petitioner is well-
connected with the hideous crime and that the trial
will be concluded within the shortest possible time
due to multiple directions already given by this
Court, therefore, he is not entitled for concession of
bail.
5. Arguments heard and record perused.
6. Tentative assessment of record reflects that the
petitioner has been apprehended in this case. The
person notified and nominated in the FIR was Raja
Muhammad Adil, son of Raja Muhammad Benares
and petitioner was not nominated directly in the FIR.
7. Prima facie, the allegation against the principal
accused was that he projected / displayed
blasphemous contents i.e. images / pictures, in
respect of “Almighty Allah, The Holy Prophet Hazrat
Muhammad ﷺ, The Holy Quran, The Holy Umhat-ul-
Momineen, Ahl-e-Bait (نيعمجا مہيلع یٰ لاعت ﷲ یضر تيب لہا) and
Sahaba Karaam (R.A)”
8. Record further reflects that this is the second
post-arrest bail application of the petitioner, whose
first post-arrest bail application was dismissed by
this Court vide order dated 22.05.2023, passed in
Crl. Misc. No.631-B-2023, whereby a direction was
issued to the learned trial Court seized with the
matter to conclude the trial within eight months. But
surprisingly, the trial has not yet been concluded,
despite the elapse of two years and eight months.
9. Now adverting to the ground of further inquiry,
I have examined the technical aspect raised by the
4
Crl. Misc. No.1956-B-2025
learned counsel for the petitioner that the original
complaint is silent regarding the nomination of the
present petitioner in any manner. This aspect has
been verified from the record by the Investigating
Officer, who is present in Court. Learned counsel
further contends that Amir Zafar, the complainant in
case No.40 of 2023, handed over the Facebook I.D.
www.facebook.com/mishakhan1122 to the I.O.
through a seizure memo dated 09.02.2023. At the
same time, the same Facebook I.D.
www.facebook.com/mishakhan1122 was taken from
Asim Mughal complainant in case FIR No.22 of 2023,
dated 18.01.2023. It has been observed from case
FIR No.22 of 2023, registered under Section 11 of
the PECA, 2016 read with Sections 295-A, 295-B,
295-C, 298-A, and 109 PPC at FIA CRC Islamabad,
that the same Facebook I.D. was used by two
different complainants for lodging two separate FIRs
against two different sets of accused persons on the
same contents, which were captured, possessed, and
taken into custody by the FIA in two separate
inquiries/criminal cases.
10. I have also gone through the seizure memo of
the online account of Amir Zafar, the complainant,
who is using the Facebook ID in the name of
“MishaKhan1122” with the same password, which
was exhibited in this criminal case as well as in
another criminal case. Such aspect outrightly
reflects that it is one set of complainant, who is
lodging multiple FIRs in these cases.
5
Crl. Misc. No.1956-B-2025
11. Learned counsel for the petitioner heavily
relied upon Criminal Petition No.1330-L of 2024
(Muhammad Omar Vs. The State), wherein the
Supreme Court of Pakistan granted post-arrest bail
to the accused while following referring paragraph 8
having following observations:
After hearing learned counsel for the petitioner and
learned AAG assisted by the Complainant, we have
perused the available record which reveals that Writ
Petition No.2667/2024 was filed in Islamabad High
Court by mother of petitioner (Noor Fatima) and others
wherein proceedings were initiated by learned Judge
of the Islamabad High Court (IHC) and vide order
dated 15th July 2025, for the detailed reasons
mentioned therein, the Federal Government has been
directed by the learned Judge of IHC to constitute a
Commission of Inquiry due to suspicion of existence of
a gang entrapping innocent citizens in cases of
blasphemy in prison without judicial or administrative
inquiry.
12. The above-mentioned aspect outrightly reflects
that the Commission of Enquiry has referred a
suspicion of existence of a gang entrapping innocent
citizens, which was a consideration for grant of bail.
13. Now considering the ground of statutory delay,
I have gone through the bail granting order of co-
accused Raja Muhammad Adil in Criminal
Miscellaneous No.1468-B-2025 dated 02.10.2025,
whereby this Court undertook a detailed exercise
from the trial Court record as well as the order sheet
in paragraph 10 of the said order, wherein 18 dates
of hearing for recording prosecution evidence were
considered for the purpose of grant of post-arrest
bail to the co-accused:
6
Crl. Misc. No.1956-B-2025
Sr.
Date Court Proceedings / Remarks
No.
1 16.05.2025 No prosecution witnesses in attendance.
2 12.06.2025 Prosecution witnesses not present.
Learned counsel for the complainant has
3 16.06.2025
requested for adjournment.
Only PW Muhammad Waseem (seizure
memo witness) present. Defence declined
4 19.06.2025
cross-exam until full recovery set is
produced. Complainant not present.
Complainant filed application claiming
mental unfitness for cross-examination,
5 21.06.2025
sought one week. No other witnesses
present.
Counsel for accused asked to cross-
examine the witness due to internet
6 24.06.2025
problem, accused could not be taken on
video link from jail
Witnesses absent. On second call, partial
7 26.06.2025 attendance but recovery memo set
incomplete.
Cross-examination of PW Nasir Rehman
8 30.06.2025 partly conducted. PW Mudassar Shah
shifted to PIMS after cardiac arrest.
Partial cross-examination of PW Nasir
9 01.07.2025 Rehman conducted. Court time ended.
PW Mudassar Shah under treatment.
10 03.07.2025 Presiding Judge on leave.
PW Nasir Rehman absent due to Lahore
11 08.07.2025 engagement. PW Mudassar Shah still
under treatment.
Prosecutor requested adjournment,
12 14.07.2025 undertook to produce case
property/documents next date.
Witnesses present but case
property/record not available (summoned
13 16.07.2025
by IHC). Defence prepared only for IO’s
cross-exam.
Examination-in-chief of PW IO Mudassar
14 22.07.2025 Shah recorded. Remaining witnesses
absent due to FIA counsel’s engagement.
Witnesses not present, direction not
15 24.07.2025
complied.
16 29.07.2025 Prosecution witnesses absent. Adjourned.
Counsel for accused appeared at 2 p.m.,
17 10.09.2025 sought re-recording of statement, request
declined.
Partial cross-examination of complainant
18 13.09.2025 PW-2 conducted. Court time ended,
adjourned to 17.09.2025.
14. However, following the aforementioned 18
dates of hearing, the trial Court conducted an
additional 18 hearings w.e.f. 13.09.2025 to
7
Crl. Misc. No.1956-B-2025
17.11.2025, which reflect that the petitioner’s
counsel cross-examined the witnesses whenever the
Court passed an order, despite the Court being on
leave on one occasion and the bar being on strike on
several other dates, as reflected in the record.
15. Surprisingly, in order dated 08.11.2025, the
trial Court observed that “at this stage, learned A.D.
Legal has pointed out that the forensic report to the
extent of accused Fahad is not available on record.
Let the I.O is directed to place the forensic report to
the extent of accused Fahad as well till next date of
hearing. Now Waseem Khan, Sabtain Ahmad Khan,
Masood Ali and Complainant be summoned for
11.11.2025.”
16. All these aspects, if seen in the context of any
delay attributable to the present petitioner, which is
not the case in hand, even then, it is a settled
proposition of law that the statutory delay period in
terms of third proviso to Section 497(1) Cr.P.C. has
to be seen in the light of case law reported as PLD
2023 SC 648 (Syeda A. Subhani Vs. The State),
wherein the primary consideration was the absence
of prosecution witnesses, absence of record or case
property, or other lapses attributable to the
prosecution and not to the accused person.
17. Similarly, the Supreme Court of Pakistan in
2024 SCMR 28 (Mahmood Usman Vs. The State)
and others) further laid down that if the accused,
after rejection of bail on the ground of delay, corrects
himself and abstains from delaying the trial but the
8
Crl. Misc. No.1956-B-2025
prosecution still fails to perform its duty in
concluding the trial, a fresh right of bail arises in his
favour, which was the main reason for grant of post-
arrest bail to the principal accused Raja Muhammad
Adil.
18. Given the above position, this Court is of the
view that the ground of further enquiry emerges on
record, and the petitioner is entitled to grant of post-
arrest bail on merit as well as on statutory delay,
whereby the pre-conviction detention period of the
petitioner exceeds 2 years and 8 months, during
which he always cooperated in the trial and cross-
examined the witnesses as and when directed by the
Court, though the delay is not directly attributable to
him on multiple occasions, as available on record.
19. Therefore, considering all these aspects along
with the principle of consistency, when the principal
accused nominated in the FIR has already been
granted post arrest bail, the petitioner has earned
his right of grant of bail. Even otherwise, the
petitioner was a student at the time of his arrest in
the University.
20. All these aspects persuade this Court to grant
bail. Consequently, the instant application is
ALLOWED, subject to furnishing bail bonds in the
sum of Rs.200,000/- with one surety in the like
amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court.
(MOHSIN AKHTAR KAYANI)
9
Crl. Misc. No.1956-B-2025
JUDGE
RAMZAN

JUDGMENT SHEET
ISLAMABAD HIGH COURT, ISLAMABAD
JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT
Criminal Revision No.116 of 2025
Muhammad Maqsood
Versus
The State and another
Petitioner by: Mr. Rehan ud Din Khan Golra,
Advocate.
Respondent No.1/State by: Mr. Muhammad Asif Khan
Jadoon, AAG along with Baber
ALI, S.I, NCCIA.
Respondent No.2 by: Mr. Imran Shafique, Advocate.
Date of Hearing: 27.10.2025.
INAAM AMEEN MINHAS, J.- Through this criminal revision, the
petitioner has assailed the order dated 21.04.2025 (“Impugned
Order”), passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge/GBV Court,
West-Islamabad (“Trial Court”), whereby the petitioner’s application
under section 265-K, Cr.P.C was dismissed.
2. The brief facts which necessitated filing of the instant criminal
revision are that the petitioner, along with co-accused disseminated
false information and incited hatred by posting toxic content including
the picture of respondent No.2/complainant Dr. Tasneem Fatima,
Associate Professor at IIUI and a video of the inquiry proceedings. The
posts were made using multiple fake social media identities. This act of
the petitioner and co-accused was allegedly carried out in retaliation of
respondent No.2’s statement disclosing malpractice by them in IIUI,
made during the meeting of the Board of Trustees of IIUI, attended by
the Chief Justice of Pakistan and the President of Pakistan/Chancellor
of IIUI. Consequently, FIR No.14/2024 dated 13.01.2024, under
2
Criminal Revision No.116 of 2025.
sections 20, 21 & 24 (d) of Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016
read with sections 419, 500, 509, 109 & 34, PPC was registered at
police station FIA/CCRC, Islamabad.
3. The petitioner was arrested on 19.03.2024. Investigation was
conducted, during which the petitioner was found involved in the
commission of the alleged offences, therefore, report under section
173, Cr.P.C. was submitted before the Court of the learned Judicial
Magistrate, Section-30, West-Islamabad on 11.09.2024, which was
subsequently entrusted to the learned Trial Court on 13.09.2024.
Copies of the documents as required under section 265-C, Cr.P.C. were
delivered to the petitioner on 07.02.2025. Thereafter, the petitioner
filed application under section 265-K, Cr.P.C, which was dismissed by
the learned Trial Court after hearing arguments of the learned counsel
for the parties vide Impugned Judgment.
4. The learned counsel for the petitioner contended that it is evident
from the record that female co-accused of the petitioner has already
been acquitted from the case under section 265-K, Cr.P.C by the
learned Trial Court on 21.04.2025 as in the forensic report no
incriminating material was found linking her with the alleged offences;
that the petitioner’s case is at par that of his female co-accused, who
has already been acquitted; that mobile of the petitioner was
confiscated and sent for forensic and the report is “Nil” as no material
evidence was found against the petitioner to connect with the alleged
offences under Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016 or PPC; that
there is no direct or circumstantial evidence against the petitioner in the
statement under section 164, Cr.P.C and continuation of the
proceedings would constitute misuse of the Court’s process; that in the
light of established Supreme Court’s precedents, where no likelihood
of conviction exists, compelling the petitioner to face trial violates his
right to a fair trial and due process under Article 10-A of the
Constitution of Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973, therefore, the
3
Criminal Revision No.116 of 2025.
Impugned Order is against the law and facts of the case.
5. On the other hand, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 fully
supported the Impugned Order and prayed for dismissal of the instant
criminal revision.
6. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused
the record.
7. As per contents of the FIR, it has been alleged that respondent
No.2 submitted a complaint before the Federal Investigation Agency
(FIA) Cyber Crime Wing against the petitioner and co-accused alleging
harassment and defamation through various social media platforms,
including Facebook and WhatsApp. Respondent No.2 asserted that the
accused persons had spread false and misleading information,
disseminated hatred and shared objectionable and toxic content
including her pictures and videos with the intenttion to damage her
reputation and cause mental distress. Upon receipt of the complaint, the
FIR was registered and after completion of the investigation, report
under section 173, Cr.P.C was submitted before the learned Trial
Court.
8. Upon careful examination of the record, it is evident that the
entire case of the prosecution against the petitioner rests upon the
allegation of circulating hateful and defamatory material against
respondent No.2 through social media platforms such as WhatsApp and
Facebook. It is the prosecution’s stance that the said act has been
committed using the petitioner’s mobile phone or laptop. During the
course of investigation, Muhammad Zubair brother of the petitioner
produced the petitioner’s mobile phone Infinix Model X682C bearing
IMEI No.354431372362268/ 354431372362276, which was taken into
possession by the Investigating Officer vide recovery memo dated
20.03.2024. The mobile phone was then forwarded to Digital Forensic
Laboratory Cyber Crime Wing, FIA Headquarters, Islamabad for
4
Criminal Revision No.116 of 2025.
digital forensic examination and extraction of any incriminating data.
After a thorough analysis, forensic report dated 28.08.2024, prepared
by Muhammad Sibtain Ahmed Khan, Assistant Director (Forensics),
conclusively found that no data or material relevant to the alleged
offences was discovered from the petitioner’s mobile phone. Therefore,
in the light of this report, it is established that the prosecution’s case
lacks corroborating digital evidence to substantiate the allegations
against the petitioner, thereby rendering the allegations unsupported by
tangible proof.
9. In cases registered under Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act,
2016 forensic report is the most vital piece of evidence, as it directly
connects or disconnects the accused from the allegations made by the
prosecution. Since the entire case of the prosecution hinges upon the
electronic evidence purportedly retrieved from the petitioner’s mobile
phone and in the absence of incriminating material, the very foundation
of the prosecution’s case collapses.
10. It is also evident from the record that the Executive Magistrate
recorded confessional statement of the petitioner under section 164,
Cr.P.C. However, upon scrutiny of its contents, it is clear that the said
statement neither contains any explicit nor implicit admission of guilt,
nor does it directly implicate the petitioner with the alleged offences.
Instead, it merely explains the allegations from the petitioner’s
perspective. It is a settled principle of law that a confessional
statement, to be relied upon for conviction, must be voluntary,
unambiguous and clearly establish the involvement of the accused with
the commission of the offences. When this statement fails to meet
essential legal standards and does not amount to a categorical
confession, it holds no evidentiary value against the petitioner.
11. It is also evident from the record that co-accused of the petitioner
namely Ms. Summiya Chughtai was charged with similar allegations
arising out of the same transaction and supported by the same set of
5
Criminal Revision No.116 of 2025.
evidence was acquitted by the learned Trial Court under section 265-K,
Cr.P.C vide order dated 21.04.2025, which order has attained finality
as neither respondent No.2 nor the State preferred any appeal against
that order. It is a well-settled principle of law that when a co-accused,
charged under the same circumstances, on the same evidence and for
the same occurrence, is acquitted and no distinguishing feature exists
then parity in law must be extended to ensure equal treatment. Since
case of the petitioner stands on the same footing as of the acquitted co-
accused in terms of allegations, evidence and parties involved, there
remains no lawful justification to treat the petitioner differently.
Therefore, the petitioner is equally entitled to the same relief.
12. In view of the evidence discussed above, it can safely be
concluded that even after recording of the evidence, there would not be
likelihood or probability of conviction of the petitioner. The learned
Trial Court has failed to properly appreciate and evaluate the material
on record in its true perspective. In these circumstances continuation of
the proceedings against the petitioner would amount to an abuse of the
process of law and would cause grave prejudice to the petitioner.
13. Under section 265-K, Cr.P.C, Trial Court has the power to acquit
an accused person even without a formal application, if it becomes
clear that there is no chance of conviction even after evidence is
recorded. The main purpose of section 265-K, Cr.P.C is to avoid
unnecessary delay and the hardship of a lengthy trial, when it is already
apparent that the accused cannot be convicted. The law allows Trial
Court to use this power at any stage of the case, whether early on, in
the middle or even towards the end of the proceedings.
14. The Honourable Supreme Court in Miraj Khan vs. Gul Ahmed
and 03 others, (2000 SCMR 122) has laid down the following dictum
regarding exercising powers under sections 249-A or 265-K of Cr.P.C:-
“The main consideration to be kept in view would be
whether the continuance of the proceedings before
6
Criminal Revision No.116 of 2025.
trial forum would be futile exercise, wastage of time
and abuse of process of Court or not. If on the basis
of the facts admitted and patent on record no offence
can be made out then it would amount to abuse of
process of law to allow the prosecution to continue
with the trial. If the facts of the present case are
scrutinize on the touch stone of the above criteria then
it would be obvious that the further proceedings in the
Court on the basis of the impugned FIR would be
sheer wastage of time.”
15. In the light of the above discussion, this criminal revision is
allowed, and Impugned Order is set aside. Consequently, application
u/s 265-K, Cr.P.C filed by the petitioner is allowed and he is acquitted
from case FIR No.14/2024 dated 13.01.2024, under sections 20, 21 &
24 (d) of Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016 read with sections
419, 500, 509, 109 & 34, PPC.
(ARBAB MUHAMMAD TAHIR) (INAAM AMEEN MINHAS)
JUDGE JUDGE
Announced in open Court on 19.11.2025.
JUDGE JUDGE
R.Anjam

ORDER SHEET
IN THE ISLAMABAD HIGH COURT, ISLAMABAD.
JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT.
Crl. Misc. No.1891-B-2025
Zeeshan Majeed Bhatti
Versus
The State and another.
S. No. of Date of Order with signature of Judge and that of parties
order/ order/ or counsel where necessary.
proceedings Proceedings
17.11.2025 Mr. Sawal Nazir Khan & Pir Asim Ullah Shah,
Advocates for petitioner.
Mr. Usman Rasool Ghumman, AAG.
Mr. M. Bilal Advocate, for CDA.
Mr. Umar Arslan, AD, FIA.
Ms. Madiha Azam, SI, FIA/CCC.
MOHSIN AKHTAR KAYANI J. Through
this Criminal Miscellaneous, the petitioner,
Zeeshan Majeed Bhatti, has prayed for his
post-arrest bail in Case FIR No.01 of 2024
dated 26.01.2024, under Section 3 / 4 Anti-
Money Laundering Act, 2010, registered at PS
FIA Anti Money Laundering Circle, Islamabad.
2. Brief facts referred in the instant FIR
are that Enquiry No. 49/2023 of the FIA Anti–
Money Laundering Circle, Islamabad,
initiated after a complaint received from the
FIA Corporate Crime Circle. The matter is
based on predicate offences already registered
in FIR No. 24/2023 dated 07.11.2023 under
2
Crl. Misc. No.1891-B-2025
sections 409, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 34,
109 PPC read with section 5(2) of the 1947
PCA. It is alleged that Ghulam Sarwar s/o
Umar Hayat (CNIC 38401-0348059-1,
resident of House 43, Street 33, Sector F-8/1,
Islamabad) in connivance with Zeeshan
Majeed Bhatti s/o Abdul Majeed Bhatti (CNIC
37405-0551973-7 (present petition), resident
of House 10-C, Street 3, Sector G-6/2,
Islamabad; cashier, L&R Directorate, CDA),
Muhammad Rafique s/o Kamal Din (CNIC
37405-0603862-7, resident of House 10,
Street 1, Quaid-e-Azam Colony, Jinnah Road,
Rawalpindi Cantt; Account Officer, L&R
Directorate, CDA) acted dishonestly and
fraudulently, with ulterior motives, and
illegally extorted Rs. 266,018,792/- by forging
the CDA record of Qabz-ul-Wasool
(Acquaintance Roll) of the legitimate claimant
Saad Masood s/o Masood Akhtar (CNIC
61101-2026734-5). They further forged Saad
Masood’s signatures, and the fraudulent
proceeds were parked/transferred into
Account No. SA-6853, titled Chaudhary
Ghulam Sarwar & Malik Saad Masood Noon,
3
Crl. Misc. No.1891-B-2025
maintained at the National Saving Centre F-8,
Islamabad. Thereafter, Ghulam Sarwar
layered/moved the proceeds of crime into
several personal and company accounts,
including but not limited to
6540061913600014 — Chaudhary Ghulam
Sarwar — BOP G-9 Islamabad,
6580061913600025 — GSG Real Estate &
Construction Co. — BOP G-9 Islamabad,
6540061913600036 — Ghulam Sarwar —
BOP G-9 Islamabad, 6580199139000018 —
GSG Real Estate & Construction Co. — BOP
G-9 Islamabad, 107000007100266 —
Chaudhary Ghulam Sarwar — U Microfinance
Bank F-7 Islamabad. The laundered proceeds
were allegedly used by Ghulam Sarwar to
acquire the following moveable/immoveable
properties:
House No. 43, Street 33, F-8/1,
Islamabad;
Plot 26, I-8 Markaz, Islamabad;
Plot 282, I-14/2, Islamabad;
Plot 1451, I-16/2, Islamabad;
Hilux Revo, Reg. No. BAG-888, Engine
No. 1GD5232636, Chassis No.
GUN126R-5556943.
4
Crl. Misc. No.1891-B-2025
It is further alleged that additional
properties acquired by the accused through
other similar predicate offences are also
under investigation by FIA Corporate Crime
Circle Islamabad. Prima facie, the acquisition
of these properties through the proceeds of
predicate offences constitutes an offence
under section 3 of the Anti-Money Laundering
Act (AMLA) 2010, punishable under section 4
of AMLA 2010, whereby, case under sections
3/4 of AMLA 2010 is being registered against
Ghulam Sarwar, Zeeshan Majeed Bhatti, and
Muhammad Rafique.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner
contends that petitioner has been nominated
as an accused in case FIR No.24 dated
07.11.2023, under sections 409, 419, 420,
467, 468, 471, 109, and 34 PPC read with
section 5 (2) of Prevention of Corruption Act
1947, registered at Police Station Cyber Crime
Circle, FIA Islamabad and was granted post-
arrest bail vide order dated 04.03.2024
through Crl. Misc. No.263-B of 2024. And as
such, there is no evidence that crime
proceeds were directly received by the
5
Crl. Misc. No.1891-B-2025
petitioner. Even the show-cause notice issued
by FIA / AMLA reflects the provisional
attachment of his property purchased by the
petitioner after receiving the alleged amount.
Hence, case of further inquiry emerges on
record.
4. Conversely, learned AAG along with the
officials of the FIA contends that petitioner
has directly received the illegal gratification
and utilized the same for purchase of the
asset which is a crime proceed and same is
apparent from his admitted record i.e. plot
number 14 sector I-12/4 Islamabad against
the consideration of Rs.73,00,000/- which
was presently freezed by the FIA authorities.
5. Arguments heard, record perused.
6. Tentative assessment of record reflects
that the co-accused in this case i.e. M. Rafiq
was granted post-arrest bail by this court in
Crl. Misc. No. 32-B of 2025 dated 21.01.2025,
while considering the role of petitioner
especially with regard to the freezing of the
asset which is allegedly purchased from the
crime proceed i.e. plot number 14 I-12/4
Islamabad. Therefore, in this regard, the FIA
6
Crl. Misc. No.1891-B-2025
authorities have secured the alleged asset.
Even otherwise, the cursory glimpse of record
further reflects that the co-accused was
granted bail and principle of consistency is
equally applicable in the present scenario.
The offence under section 3/4 AMLA, 2010,
entails the sentence of not less than 1 year
but may extend up to 10 years and shall also
be liable to fine which may extend up to
Rs.25 Million and shall also be liable for
forfeiture of property involved in money
laundering or a property of corresponding
value. If such aspect has been considered as
a primary factor, it appears that there are two
different sentences that have been given with
minimum threshold which out rightly leads
this case into a non-prohibitory clause of
section 497 Cr.P.C. Hence, instant post-arrest
bail application is ALLOWED, subject to
furnishing bail bonds in the sum of
Rs.100,000/- with one surety in the like amount
to the satisfaction of learned trial.
(MOHSIN AKHTAR KAYANI)
JUDGE
A.Waheed/-

ORDER SHEET
IN THE ISLAMABAD HIGH COURT, ISLAMABAD.
JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT.
Crl. Misc. No.1809-B-2025
Muhammad Abdullah Shoaib
Versus
The State and another.
S. No. of Date of Order with signature of Judge and that of parties
order/ order/ or counsel where necessary.
proceedings Proceedings
03.11.2025 Mr. Talha Sarfraz, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Usman Rasool Ghumman, AAG.
Mr. Adil Aziz Qazi, Mr. M. Yaseen Iqbal & Rao
Abdur Raheem, Advocates for respondent
No.2.
Mr. Asif Nawaz, Deputy Director, & Mr. Aazim
Shahjahan, Insepctor, NCCIA, CCRC,
Islamabad.
MOHSIN AKHTAR KAYANI J. Through
this Criminal Miscellaneous, the petitioner,
Muhammad Abdullah Shoaib, has prayed for
his post-arrest bail in Case FIR No.12 of 2023
dated 10.01.2023 under Section 11 of the
Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016 read
with Sections 295-A, 295-B, 295-C, 298-A, and
109 PPC, registered at PS FIA Cyber Crime
Circle, Islamabad.
2. Brief facts, referred in the instant FIR
lodged on the complaint of Abdullah Sultan,
are that the complainant has alleged, based on
2
Crl. Misc. No.1809-B-2025
material obtained from social media platforms
Facebook and WhatsApp, that some unknown
persons are operating in groups from their
Facebook account IDs referred as
(https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=10
0076580230671,https://www.facebook.com/u
mair.alisaleem.3, 923020041329, and
923162946070) and are illegally and
unauthorizedly creating, developing, uploading,
and transmitting publicly displayed
blasphemous content, images, and pictures.
The complaint was converted into an FIR,
whereby the present petitioner was nominated
by the FIA and the investigation has been
completed.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner
inter alia contends that the petitioner was not
nominated in the original complaint; however,
he was later on nominated by the FIA. As such,
nothing incriminating has been recovered from
the petitioner. Even the FIA has not verified the
complainant’s account or the details of his
Facebook account, mobile number, or any
other ID through which it could be ascertained
that the complainant ever received any
3
Crl. Misc. No.1809-B-2025
blasphemous content on his ID. It has further
been argued that the complainant submitted
his Facebook ID as
https://www.facebook.com/laibaking12/, which
was also part of three other FIRs lodged in a
similar manner by different complainants
against different accused persons. The counsel
contends that the petitioner is behind the bars
since 10.01.2023 and has spent almost two
years and eleven months, and so far, the trial
has not been concluded due to the delay
caused by the prosecution in this case.
4. Conversely, learned AAG, as well as
counsel for the complainant and the
Investigating Officer, opposed the instant post-
arrest bail application on the ground that the
forensic report verified the blasphemous
content from the login ID of the petitioner and,
as such, he is directly connected with the this
hideous crime.
5. Arguments heard, record perused.
6. Tentative assessment of record
reflects that the petitioner was not directly
nominated in the complaint filed by the
complainant Abdullah Sultan, which is evident
4
Crl. Misc. No.1809-B-2025
from the contents of the complaint, where two
Facebook IDs with two different mobile
numbers have been referred. However, the
technical forensic expert report confirms the
following findings:
“No sharing of WhatsApp account i.e.
+923020041329 has been found.”
This report has been exhibited in
evidence as Exhibit PW-2/B/1-13 before the
trial court. Such an aspect confirms that the
mobile number recovered from the petitioner
was not used for any sharing of blasphemous
content.
7. Similarly, another important aspect
has been noticed, whereby the complaint filed
by the respondent/complainant only states two
Facebook accounts and two IDs without
referring to his own Facebook account, ID, or
number. The seizure memo of the online
account in this FIR, Exhibit PW-1/A, reflects
the Facebook URL:
https://www.facebook.com/libaking12. The
description gives login ID:
mk8141820@gmail.com with password:
Liba0245, which was seized in this case.
5
Crl. Misc. No.1809-B-2025
However, in another case FIR No. 188 of 2022
PS FIA Cybercrime was reported with similar
allegations by a complainant, and in that FIR,
the seizure memo also reflects the same ID.
Likewise, a third FIR No. 24 of 2023 lodged by
one Imran Farooq with similar allegations also
reflects the same Facebook ID with the same
login and password. Such an aspect confirms
that the same Facebook account and ID have
been used by three different complainants in
three different FIRs against three different sets
of accused persons. Despite that, the FIA
authorities have made a single seizure memo of
the complainant’s Facebook ID, and no
restriction has been imposed, nor any
explanation rendered by the Investigating
Officer as to how the same Facebook ID has
been used by three different complainants.
Such an aspect, if considered in the context of
W.P. No. 2667 of 2024 filed in the Islamabad
High Court, whereby one Noor Fatima, mother
of an accused, made a request to constitute a
Commission of Inquiry due to suspicion of the
existence of a gang entrapping innocent
citizens in cases of blasphemy with ulterior
6
Crl. Misc. No.1809-B-2025
motives, improper investigation, and the death
of four accused of blasphemy in prison without
judicial or administrative inquiry, which fact
was duly recorded in the order dated
25.09.2025 passed in Criminal Petition
No.1330-L of 2024 titled “Muhammad Umar
versus The State” by the Supreme Court of
Pakistan, whereby the accused persons were
granted post-arrest bail on this single count.
As such, all these aspects cumulatively
disclose a factum of further inquiry in favour of
the petitioner. Even otherwise, I have
confronted the Investigating Officer to confirm
the ID of the petitioner with respect to the
mobile number, whereby he contends that the
accused is not the owner of the recovered
mobile number. The same is the position with
the complainant’s Facebook ID, for which the
Investigating Officer conceded before the Court
that till date, the Facebook ID of the
complainant as well as the number have not
been verified, as the same is required to be
verified by Meta, the company which is not in
Pakistan. Moreover, not a single statement
under Section 161 Cr.P.C. was referred in
7
Crl. Misc. No.1809-B-2025
which the complainant owns the Facebook ID
through which he received any blasphemous
content. In such an aspect, the ground of
further inquiry in terms of Subsection (2) of
Section 497 Cr.P.C. emerges on record.
8. I have also confronted the
Investigating Officer present in Court to
authenticate those blasphemous content
pictures as to whether they are genuine or
doctored, and whether they were created by the
petitioner and transmitted to others. However,
the Investigating Officer was unable to
demonstrate from any record that the pictures
allegedly referred to are the handiwork of the
petitioner. Such an aspect is also a ground of
further inquiry. Besides these aspects, this
Court is of the view, by comparing all the
blasphemous content which is similar in all
other cases presented before this Court in
different FIRs, that when the Investigating
Officer has conceded that the petitioner is not
the author nor the creator of any blasphemous
content, the primary allegation is required to
be established in the trial court.
8
Crl. Misc. No.1809-B-2025
9. I have also gone through the record
and convinced that the entire case has been
proceeded in violation of Section 156 Cr.P.C.
and Section 196 Cr.P.C., and no record of the
cellular service provider is available, nor the
subscriber of the SIM. All such scenarios
create doubt. Besides this, the petitioner is
behind the bars for two years and eleven
months, and the trial has not yet been
concluded. In this backdrop, the petitioner has
earned his bail both on merit as well as on
account of statutory delay, in which no lawful
justification has been rendered from the
prosecution side as to why the instant case has
not been concluded. Therefore, considering all
these aspects as well as the allegations
contained in this case, a tentative assessment
is made by this Court, as it is not permissible
to go into the details of the evidence in any
manner which might prejudice either party.
However, it is also a settled law that the
heinousness of the offence alone is not
sufficient to deprive the Court of its discretion
to grant bail, which is never refused as
punishment. There is no legal or moral
9
Crl. Misc. No.1809-B-2025
compulsion to keep a person incarcerated
merely because of the severity of the charge.
Hence, considering the mandate of PLD 1972
[SC] 81 (Manzoor Vs. State) and 2016 SCMR
18 (Zaigham Ashraf Vs. State), instant post-
arrest bail application is ALLOWED, subject to
furnishing bail bonds in the sum of
Rs.200,000/- with one surety in the like amount
to the satisfaction of learned trial court with an
additional amount of Rs.50,000/- to be
deposited in the trial court account as surety
to ensure the petitioner’s presence before the
trial court till the conclusion of the trial.
(MOHSIN AKHTAR KAYANI)
JUDGE
A.Waheed/-

ORDER-SHEET
IN THE ISLAMABADHIGH COURT, ISLAMABAD
JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT
Criminal Misc. No.1432-B of 2025
Mehran Ali
Versus
The State, etc.
S. No. of Date of Order with signature of Judge and that of
order/ order/ parties or counsel where necessary.
proceedings Proceedings
30.10.2025 Raja Talha Sarfraz Khan, Advocate for petitioner,
Mr. Khurram Mehmood Qureshi, Advocate for the
respondent,
Mr. Muhammad Sajid Khan Tanoli, DAG,
Mr. Mudasir Shah, DD-FIA,
Mr. Asif Nawaz DD(L) NCCIA,
Ms. Azram Shahjahan, Inspector, NCCIA.
Arbab Muhammad Tahir, J: By way of listed
criminal miscellaneous in terms of 3rd proviso to section
497 Cr. P.C, petitioner namely Mehran Ali prays for post-
arrest bail in FIR No.132, dated 19.07.2023, under section
11 of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016 read
with sections 295-A, 295-B, 295-C, 298-A and 109 PPC,
Police Station FIA Cyber Crime Circle, Islamabad, on
statutory ground of delay in conclusion of trial.
2. Heard. It is well settled that in order to avail
remedy under 3rd proviso to section 497 Cr. P.C, it is
obligatory for an accused to show that the delay in
conclusion of trial has not been occasioned due to his fault
or the fault of his pleader, as the case may be.
3. When confronted, learned DAG apprised that the
examination-in-chief of three witnesses has since been
recorded but the learned defense counsel has not yet
cross-examined them and that the prosecution is ready to
produce all the prosecution witnesses for recording of their
statements. It is, thus obvious that petitioner cannot be
absolved of liability of causing delay in conclusion of trial at
2
Crl. Misc. No. 1432-B-2025
the earliest, therefore, listed criminal is dismissed with
direction to the trial court to conclude the trial of the
subject case within a period of 01 month from the receipt
of copy of this order. It is expected that learned counsel for
the parties shall extend full cooperation with the trial court
for achieving the task.
4. Copy of this order shall be transmitted to the
learned DAG with direction to ensure the production of all
the prosecution witnesses before the trial court on the date
fixed. The court concerned be informed accordingly.
(ARBAB MUHAMMAD TAHIR)
JUDGE
Shafqat

ORDER SHEET
IN THE ISLAMABAD HIGH COURT, ISLAMABAD.
JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT.
Crl. Misc. No.1780-B-2025
Zeeshan Ahmed
Versus
The State and another.
Crl. Misc. No.1836-B-2025
Muhammad Tooqer
Versus
The State and another.
Crl. Misc. No.1837-B-2025
Usman Bashir
Versus
The State and another.
S. No. of Date of Order with signature of Judge and that of parties or
order/ order/ counsel where necessary.
proceedings Proceedings
(04) 29.10.2025 Mr. Asif Ali Tamboli, Mr. Hadi Ali Chatha,
Advocates for the petitioners in their respective
petitions.
Mr. Usman Rasool Ghumman, AAG.
Mr. Adil Aziz Qazi, Advocate for respondent No.2.
Asif Nawaz, D.D NCCIA CCRC/F.I.A, Islamabad.
Asim Shahjehan, Inspector, CCRC, F.I.A,
Islamabad.
MOHSIN AKHTAR KAYANI J. By way of this
common order, I intend to decide all the captioned
petitions arisen out of the same F.I.R.
2. Through these petitions, the petitioners have
applied for post arrest bail in case FIR No.188/22,
dated 30.11.2022, under Section 11 of PECA 2016
read with Sections 295-A, 295-B, 295-C, 298-A &
109 PPC, F.I.A Cyber Crime Circle, Islamabad.
3. Brief facts referred in the instant FIR are that
an inquiry was initiated on the complaint of Hafiz
2
Crl. Misc. No.1780-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1836-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1837-B-2025
Liaqat Manzoor Combo by the FIR whereby accused
Usman Bashir user of whatsapp account
No.+923239197814 and Facebook Profile having
URL:www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=1000840019
04266, with criminal intention and ulterior motive
illegally and unauthorizedly, created/developed and
further uploaded/transmitted/disseminated as well
as publicly projected/displayed Holy and Sacred
name of The Almighty Allah, The Holy Quran Majeed
and Ahl e Bait R.A on private parts of the human
naked body alongwith sacrilegious, loathsome
narration/speech, using Whatsapp
No.+02329197814 and Facebook profile having URL
www.facebook.come/profile.php?id=1000840019042
66, by participating within different Facebook
profiles and whatsapp account/groups and willfully
defiled and outraged religious feelings, belief as well
as spirit of Islam. During the investigation, the
alleged Facebook Account alongwith the electronic
devices were recovered from the accused persons
being used in the commission of above referred
offences. Hence this F.I.R
4. Learned counsel for petitioner Zeeshan Ahmed
contends that he has not been nominated in the
instant FIR and was later on involved in this case.
He further contends that the instant post-arrest bail
application is the second post-arrest bail application
of accused Zeeshan Ahmed, whose earlier post-arrest
3
Crl. Misc. No.1780-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1836-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1837-B-2025
bail application, Criminal Miscellaneous No. 251-B
of 2023, was dismissed vide order dated 13.03.2023.
As such, the petitioner has spent 02 years and 10
months (equal to 34 months) behind the bars, and
till date not a single prosecution witness has been
cross-examined, despite the fact that a direction was
also issued to the trial Court by the Hon’ble Supreme
Court of Pakistan in Criminal Petition No.586 of
2023 and Criminal Miscellaneous Application No.769
of 2023 titled Zeeshan Ahmed Vs. The State vide
order dated 15.06.2023 to expedite the trial. He
further contends that 7 PWs have been recorded only
for examination-in-chief, but on majority of hearing
dates in the Trial Court, adjournments were granted
due to non-availability of prosecution witnesses. The
period of statutory delay is already over, and the
petitioner is not a contributing factor for non-
conclusion of trial. He further contends that certain
grounds were not taken in the previous post-arrest
bail application, especially the reference to the
forensic report, which was not taken into account in
the previous order. As such, he is not directly linked
with the heinous crime mentioned in the Challan. He
further contends that no proof of ownership of the
mobile number was thrashed out in investigation
and even the complainant in his complaint has not
referred the conduct of the petitioner in any manner.
It is not even the case of the prosecution that the
4
Crl. Misc. No.1780-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1836-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1837-B-2025
petitioner is the author or creator of any
blasphemous content. He further argues that no
forensic report is available with regard to the mobile
phone or Facebook account of the complainant in
this case to corroborate the role of the petitioner.
5. Learned counsel for petitioners Muhammad
Touqeer and Usman Basheer contends that though the
name of Usman Basheer is though referred in the FIR,
it was not mentioned in the complaint, and the FIR
has been transmitted with his name. He further
contends that both petitioners have filed their first
post-arrest bail applications. Petitioner Muhammad
Touqeer was arrested on 03.03.2023, while
petitioner Usman Basheer was apprehended on
30.11.2022, and as such, they have spent almost
two and a half years in jail and their trial has not
yet been concluded. He further contends that the
petitioners were not able to engage counsel, and even
the Trial Court did not pass any direction to engage
defence counsel on their behalf, which further
negates the rights of the petitioners. It is further
contended that the record and complaint clearly
reflect that both mobile numbers referred by the
prosecution in connection with sharing the
blasphemous contents did not belong to the
present petitioners, and this aspect has been
admitted in the final report. He further contends
that no SIM was recovered from Muhammad
5
Crl. Misc. No.1780-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1836-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1837-B-2025
Touqeer to synchronize the allegations with
respect to any mobile number, nor has any
forensic report proved to link the petitioner with this
case. He further submits that one of the petitioners,
Muhammad Touqeer, was a student of Fouji
Foundation College, studying DAE (Electrical), and
was 19 years of age, whereas petitioner Usman
Basheer was a daily wager. As such, after the lapse
of the statutory period, they are entitled to the
concession of post-arrest bail accordingly.
6. Conversely, learned counsel for the
complainant contends that petitioner Zeeshan
Ahmed is not entitled to concession of bail on merits
as his first post-arrest bail application was
dismissed by this Court and upheld by the
Honourable Supreme Court of Pakistan. He further
contends that all three accused are to be seen in the
light of the orders passed by this Court as well as
the Supreme Court on the principle of consistency,
as their roles are equal. He further contends that the
FIA has submitted the Challan, charge was framed,
and seven prosecution witnesses have been recorded
to the extent of their examination-in-chief, but they
have never been cross-examined by the
petitioners/accused. The trial has been delayed only
due to the conduct of the petitioners. He submits
that if a direction is issued to the Trial Court to
conclude the trial by completing the cross-
6
Crl. Misc. No.1780-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1836-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1837-B-2025
examination of the prosecution witnesses, the matter
can be decided within 10 to 15 days.
7. Arguments heard and record perused.
8. Tentative assessment of record reflects that all
three petitioners, namely Zeeshan Ahmed,
Muhammad Touqeer, and Usman Basheer, have not
been nominated in the complaint filed by respondent
No.2. The complaint filed by Hafiz Liaquat Manzoor
Kamboh, Advocate, is of general nature, reflecting 16
mobile numbers with two Facebook account IDs,
referring to a single person namely Tariq, alleged to
outraging the religious sentiments of every Muslim in
Pakistan by uploading, transmitting, disseminating,
and publicly displaying holy and sacred names of
Almighty Allah, the Holy Qur’an, and Ahl-e-Bayt on
private parts of human bodies, along with
sacrilegious and loathsome narration/speech, using
WhatsApp and Facebook accounts.
9. However, when the FIR was registered, it
surprisingly included the name of Usman Basheer,
one of the petitioners. This aspect was confronted to
the Investigation Officer (IO), who stated that Usman
Basheer was the first accused arrested in this case
on 30.11.2022, whereas Touqeer was arrested on
03.03.2023 and Zeeshan Ahmed on 30.12.2022. A
final report was submitted after obtaining the
forensic report from the FIA. He further contends
7
Crl. Misc. No.1780-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1836-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1837-B-2025
that all accused have been connected with the
serious offence of sharing blasphemous content.
10. During the course of arguments, it appears
that all three petitioners are prima facie not the
authors or creators of any of the blasphemous
content, and this aspect has been conceded by the
Investigation Officer, who stated that different
images were shared through different WhatsApp
numbers and Facebook accounts.
11. A surprising fact surfaced on record is that the
alleged mobile numbers used by Touqeer and Usman
were actually in the names of Nighat Shaheen and
Gulzar, but the I.O. did not investigate these two
individuals. Hence, a case of further inquiry emerges
on record to the extent of these two accused persons.
Even otherwise, petitioner Touqeer was a student of
Fauji Foundation College, studying DAE (Electrical)
at the time of arrest and was 19 years of age,
whereas petitioner Usman Basheer, aged 27 years,
was a labourer from AJK.
12. All these aspects are seen in the context of the
forensic reports. It appears that there is no direct
evidence connecting these two petitioners with the
creation of the blasphemous contents. Even the I.O.
acknowledged that all copies of blasphemous
contents referred in the record are similar and have
been used in multiple cases where separate FIRs
have been lodged against different individuals.
8
Crl. Misc. No.1780-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1836-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1837-B-2025
13. Now adverting to the case of Zeeshan Ahmed,
who filed the instant post-arrest bail application for
the second time after the lapse of approximately two
and a half years, his first bail application was
dismissed on 13.03.2023 and upheld by the Hon’ble
Supreme Court of Pakistan in Criminal Petition
No.586 of 2023 and Criminal Miscellaneous
Application No.769 of 2023 titled Zeeshan Ahmed Vs.
The State), decided on 15.06.2023, whereby the
Hon’ble Supreme Court directed the Trial Court to
expedite the trial and decide the matter
expeditiously. However, till date, the trial has not yet
been concluded.
14. Perusal of the order sheet reveals that the Trial
Court attended the case on 46–47 hearing dates, out
of which prosecution evidence was not available on
approximately 21 dates, whereas on 22 dates, delay
is attributed to the accused side. Primarily, the
accused persons, namely Usman Basheer,
Muhammad Asif Khan Lodi, Muhammad Shahzad,
Muhammad Tariq, and Zeeshan Ahmed, remained
unrepresented for more than two years. Only one
counsel was appointed by accused Muhammad
Touqeer. Even on one occasion, the Trial Court
passed the following order:
“In the interest of justice, adjournment is granted. If learned
defence counsel does not cross-examine the witnesses on the
next date of hearing, counsel at state expense would be
appointed.”
9
Crl. Misc. No.1780-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1836-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1837-B-2025
15. This order was passed on 27.11.2024, but even
after its passing, the Trial Court did not appoint any
defence counsel for all accused. This aspect is not
understandable as to why the Court did not adopt
the approach to conclude the trial by appointing a
counsel at state expense. Two of the accused have
now been represented in the Trial Court through
counsel appointed only in June 2025.
16. When this aspect was confronted, learned
counsel for the petitioners contended that the
majority of petitioners were not able to engage their
own counsel and had only hired counsel for the post-
arrest bail proceedings, even majority of counsels are
afraid to be engaged in these types of cases.
17. This Court has also summoned a report from
the learned Trial Court regarding the progress of the
trial, whereby a report dated 29.10.2025 reflects that
no prosecution witnesses was in attendance on the
last five dates of hearing i.e. 16.06.2025,
17.07.2025, 17.09.2025, 18.10.2025, and
21.10.2025. Although some of the witnesses were
present whose examination-in-chief had earlier been
recorded, but they were not cross-examined. It has
specifically been mentioned that Mr. Hadi Ali Chatta,
Advocate, submitted a fresh vakalatnama on behalf
of accused Muhammad Tauqir in May 2025.
Therefore, the ground raised by the petitioner,
Zeeshan, regarding the delay in conclusion of the
10
Crl. Misc. No.1780-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1836-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1837-B-2025
trial appears to be justified. Furthermore, from the
perusal of the report, it is evident that the delay is
attributable to the prosecution, and there is no
likelihood of an early conclusion of the trial.
18. In this backdrop, this Court has considered
the law laid down in 2024 SCMR 28 (Muhammad
Usman Vs. The State), wherein it has been held
that:
The right of an accused to seek bail on statutory
grounds cannot be defeated for any other reason
except those explicitly described under the third
and fourth provisos to Section 497(1) Cr.P.C. The
accused becomes entitled to bail as of right after
the statutory period expressly stated in clauses (a)
and (b), as the case may be, has expired and the
trial has not concluded.
This accrual of right is manifest from the language
of the third proviso. Such right can only be defeated
if the prosecution is able to show that delay in the
trial was attributable to an act or omission of the
accused or a person acting on his behalf. If the
prosecution succeeds in showing to the satisfaction
of the Court that the accused was at fault, then the
right stands forfeited. It has been held that the
right recognized under the third proviso to Section
497(1) cannot be denied to an accused on the basis
of discretionary powers of the Court. The right is
not left to the discretion of the Court; rather, its
accrual is subject to fulfillment of the conditions
mentioned in the third proviso.
19. Moreover, while calculating the quantum of
delay attributable to an accused, the Court is
required to consider whether or not the progress and
conclusion of the trial were delayed by the act or
11
Crl. Misc. No.1780-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1836-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1837-B-2025
omission of the accused. While ascertaining delay,
cumulative facts and disposal of the case have to be
considered, and its assessment cannot be
determined mathematically by merely excluding
those dates for which adjournments were sought by
the accused. The main factor for consideration is the
attendance of witnesses and whether, despite the
matter having become ripe for evidence, delay was
caused by the accused.
20. The recording of the statement of the last
witness would also not defeat the right recognized
under the third proviso. Reference may be made to
1983 SCMR 72 (Nazir Hussain Vs. Ziaul Haq),
1998 SCMR 190 (Sher Ali Sheri Vs. The State),
PLD 1982 SC 424 (Abbas Vs. The State), PLD
1990 SC 934 (Moundar Vs. The State), 1998
SCMR 897 (Abdul Rashid Vs. The State), PLD
1995 SC 49 (Zahid Hussain Shah Vs. The State),
1998 PCr.LJ 358 (Muhammad Siddique Vs.
Muhammad Behram and another).
21. On the analogy discussed above, this Court is
of the view that delay is not attributable to petitioner
Zeeshan Ahmed, who has earned his right to grant of
post-arrest bail on the basis of statutory delay,
especially when no counsel was appointed by the
Trial Court despite clear order, and the petitioner
remained incarcerated for more than two years
without conclusion of trial, even in the presence of
12
Crl. Misc. No.1780-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1836-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1837-B-2025
the direction passed by the Honourable Supreme
Court of Pakistan.
22. Even otherwise, it is not possible, as claimed
by the respondent side, that direction be issued for
conclusion of trial within 15–16 days, for the main
reason that the petitioners should have been
represented through counsel appointed at state
expense. Since this was not done by the Trial Court,
an exception comes on record, and statutory delay,
considering the entire Trial Court order sheet, gives
rise to a scenario where the petitioners were not
compelled to cross-examine witnesses by themselves
nor any direction was given in this regard by the trial
Court. In such absence, the statutory right to bail on
grounds of delay comes into play, and petitioner
Zeeshan Ahmed is entitled to the concession of bail.
23. During arguments, learned counsel for
petitioners also relied upon the order dated
25.09.2025 passed by the Honourable Supreme
Court of Pakistan in Criminal Petition No. 1330-L of
2024, Muhammad Omar vs. The State, in a criminal
case relating to offences of blasphemy with PECA,
wherein the Supreme Court referred Writ Petition
No.2667 of 2024 filed before the Islamabad High
Court by one of the accused for appointment of a
Commission of Enquiry due to suspicion of existence
of a gang entrapping innocent citizens in blasphemy
cases, improper investigation, and deaths of four
13
Crl. Misc. No.1780-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1836-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1837-B-2025
accused in prison without judicial or administrative
enquiry. Considering all these aspects, the Supreme
Court granted post-arrest bail in similar
circumstances.
24. Both sides have also argued with reference to
Section 196 Cr.P.C., where criminal proceedings
have been carried out in breach of the obligation
provided under the Cr.P.C. as held in PLD 2024 SC
681 (Zubair Saeed Sabri/Sain Zubair Shah Vs.
The State) and PLD 2022 SC 751 (Salamat
Mansha Masih vs. The State).
25. It is also a settled principle of law that while
deciding a bail application before conclusion of trial,
only tentative assessment is to be made by the
Court, and it is not permissible to go into the details
of evidence in a manner that might prejudice either
party, as held in 2021 SCMR 111 (Imtiaz Vs. Azam
Khan) and 2020 SCMR 937 (Bilal Khan Vs. The
State). It is also settled law that heinousness of the
offence alone is not sufficient to deprive the Court of
its discretion to grant bail, which is never refused as
punishment. There is no legal or moral compulsion
to keep a person incarcerated merely because of the
severity of the charge.
26. The ultimate conviction and incarceration of a
guilty person can repair the wrong caused by
mistaken relief of bail after arrest, but no
satisfactory reparation can be offered to an accused
14
Crl. Misc. No.1780-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1836-B-2025
Crl. Misc. No.1837-B-2025
for his unjustified incarceration if ultimately
acquitted. Reliance is placed on PLD 1972 SC 81
Manzoor Ahmed and 04 others Vs. The State) and
2016 SCMR 18 (Zaigham Ashraf Vs. The State).
27. For what has been discussed above, all the
captioned petitions are ALLOWED and petitioner
Zeeshan Ahmed is granted post-arrest bail on the
ground of statutory delay, whereas petitioners
Muhammad Touqeer and Usman Basheer are
granted post-arrest bail on merit as well as on
statutory delay, subject to furnishing bail bonds in
the sum of Rs.200,000/- each with one surety each
in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial
Court. They are further directed to deposit a cash
amount of Rs.50,000/- each in the Trial Court’s
account as surety, to ensure their appearance before
the Trial Court till conclusion of the trial
accordingly.
(MOHSIN AKHTAR KAYANI)
JUDGE
RAMZAN

before: Honourable Mr. Justice Arbab Muhammad Tahir, Honourable Mr. Justice Inaam Ameen Minhas

under section 3(2) of the Law Reforms

judgment_link: https://mis.ihc.gov.pk/frmRdJgmnt.aspx?cseNo=Intra Court Appeal-362-2025 | -&cseTle=Muhammad Uzair Anwar VS Fop etc&jgs=Honourable Mr. Justice Arbab Muhammad Tahir, Honourable Mr. Justice Inaam Ameen Minhas&jgmnt=/attachments/judgements/202173/1/202173_638974332913266512.pdf

Form No: HCJD/C-121
ORDER SHEET
IN THE ISLAMABAD HIGH COURT, ISLAMABAD
(JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT)
I.C.A. No.362-2025
Muhammad Uzair Anwar and others
Versus
Federation of Pakistan and others
Appellants by : Barrister Abdul Qadeer, Advocate
(in ICA No.362-2025)
Barrister Abdul Ahad Khokher,
Advocate (in ICA No.360-2025)
Mr Muhammad Fiaz Kandwal,
Advocate (in ICA No.359-2025)
Barrister Mian Ali Ashfaq,
Advocate (in ICA No.361-2025)
Respondents by : Mr Asif Jadoon, AAG.
Mr Wasi Ullah Khan, Advocate
for BoP.
Date of Hearing : 15.10.2025
Arbab Muhammad Tahir, J.- Through this
consolidated judgment we will decide the instant
appeal alongwith the following connected matters.-
(i). ICA No.359-2025, Sajid Nadeem v.
Federation of Pakistan and othes
(ii). ICA No.360-2025, Makhdoom
Muhammad Shahab Ud Din and others
v. Federation of Pakistan and others
(iii). ICA No.361-2025, Orya Maqbool Abbasi
and others v. Federation of Pakistan and
others
2. The appellants, through the Intra Court
Appeals preferred under section 3(2) of the Law Reforms
Ordinance, 1972 have impugned consolidated judgment
dated 11.08.2025 passed by the learned Single Judge
Page-2
ICAs No.359, 360, 361 & 362 of 2025
whereby Writ Petitions No.2883, 2882, 2884 & 2885 of
2025 filed by the appellants were dismissed.
3. The relevant facts, per the record, are that
any inquiry was initiated by National Cyber Crime
Investigating Agency (hereinafter ‗NCCIA‘) on a source
report that appellants are involved in online activities in
breach of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016
(hereinafter the ‗2016-Act‘). During pendency of the
inquiry, the NCCIA forwarded requests to different Banks
to freeze the Bank accounts of the appellants, which were
acted upon accordingly. The appellants filed writ petitions
seeking the relief that the directives issued to the Banks
by the NCCIA for freezing of their Bank accounts be
declared without lawful authority. The said petitions were
dismissed by the learned Single Judge vide the impugned
consolidated judgment dated 11.08.2025, hence these
Intra Court Appeals.
4. Learned counsel for the for the appellants
have argued that the impugned action of the NCCIA is
violative of rights of appellants protected under Articles 4,
10A, 19, 24 & 24A of the Constitution; that the appellants
were not confronted with any incriminating material before
initiating the request of freezing of their Bank accounts;
that penalizing the whole families for the alleged wrong of
one person is unconstitutional; that the NCCIA is not
vested with any power to request Banks for freezing of
Bank accounts of citizens; that the impugned order is
liable to be set aside.
5. Conversely, learned Assistant Attorney
General has argued that the NCCIA is empowered to
request the Banks for freezing of the Bank accounts of
Page-3
ICAs No.359, 360, 361 & 362 of 2025
citizens allegedly involved in activities in breach of the
provisions of 2016-Act; the impugned order is well
reasoned; the appeals are liable to be dismissed.
6. Heard. Record perused.
7. The appellants‟ Bank accounts were frozen by
the Banks pursuant to the request of the NCCIA on the
grounds that allegedly they are involved in ‗uploading of
Anti State Contents/Posts on social media and are selling
sensitive information to various foreign entities as well as
spreading false and misleading information to general
public‘. The reasons which prevailed with the learned
Single Judge to dismissed the constitutional petitions are
that under the provisions of Anti-Money Laundering Act,
2010 (hereinafter ‗2010-Act‘) the NCCIA is empowered to
order freezing of the Bank accounts coupled with the
powers conferred by the provisions of the 2016-Act.
8. In order to address the questions of law raised
for our consideration, it would be appropriate to briefly
survey the legislative scheme under which the NCCIA
exercises its authority.
9. The NCCIA was formerly known as the
National Response Centre for Cyber Crimes (NR3C), a
subordinate wing of the Federal Investigation Agency. The
NCCIA enjoyed the legal cover under the Federal
Investigation Agency Act, 1974 (hereinafter ‗1974-Act‘),
which inter alia, included the powers under section 5 of
the 1974-Act. The then NR3C enjoyed the powers
simultaneously under the two statutes i.e. 2016-Act as
well as 1974-Act. Relevant to the case in hand is the
Page-4
ICAs No.359, 360, 361 & 362 of 2025
power under sub section (5) of section 5 of the 1974-Act,
which reads as under.-
―If, in the opinion of a member of the Agency
conducting an investigation, any property which is
the subject-matter of the investigation is likely to
be removed, transferred or otherwise disposed of
before an order of the appropriate authority for its
seizure is obtained, such member may, by order in
writing, direct the owner or any person who is, for
the time being, possession thereof not to remove,
transfer or otherwise dispose of such property in
any manner except with the previous permission of
that member and such order shall be subject to
any order made by the Court having jurisdiction in
the matter.‖
(Highlighted to add emphasis)
It is significant to mention that the expression
„Agency‟ is defined in section 2(1) of the 1974-Act as
meaning the Federal Investigation Agency constituted
under section 3 thereof. Section 3 of the 1974-Act is
reproduced below.-
―3. Constitution of the Agency:
1. Notwithstanding anything contained in
any other law of the time being in force,
the Federal Government may constitute
an Agency to be called the Federal
Investigation Agency for inquiry into, and
investigation of the offences specified in
the Schedule, including an attempt or
conspiracy to commit, and abetment of,
any such offence.
2. The Agency shall consist of a Director
General to be appointed by the Federal
Government and such number of other
officers as the Federal Government may,
from time to time, appoint to be
members of the Agency.‖
It is thus clear from the above, that the
powers conferred by section 5 of the 1974-Act (freezing of
the Bank accounts/property) are exclusively vested in the
officers of the “Agency” i.e. the Federal Investigation
Agency.
Page-5
ICAs No.359, 360, 361 & 362 of 2025
10. Subsequently, the 2016-Act was amended by
Prevention of Electronic Crimes (Amendment) Act, 2025
(the ‗Amendment Act‘). By virtue of section 6 of the
Amendment Act, section 29 of the 2016-Act was
substituted; sub section (1) whereof provides that the
Federal Government shall establish an investigation
agency to be called the National Cyber Crimes
Investigation Agency (NCCIA). In pursuance of section
29(5), the Federal Government vide S.R.O. 748(I)/2025,
dated 29.04.2025 has duly established the NCCIA for
investigation of the offences under the 2016-Act. For the
sake of convenience, the same is reproduced below.-
―S.R.O. 748(I)/2025.- In exercise of powers
conferred by section 29 of the Prevention of
Electronic Crimes Act, 2016 (XL of 2016) read with
sub-section (5) thereof, the Federal Government is
pleased to establish the National Cyber Crime
Investigation Agency for the purposes of
Investigation of the offences under the said Act
w.e.f. 04-04-2025.‖
This demonstrates that the NCCIA is now an
independent body and no more a subordinate office of the
Federal Investigation Agency and has thus stripped of the
powers under the 1974-Act, particularly section 5(5)
thereof.
11. The NCCIA derives its existence and authority
from the 2016-Act. This signifies that the NCCIA shall
exercise only those powers, which are delegated to it by
the Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) through the 2016-Act.
Likewise, in terms of section 2(xviii) of section 2 of the
2010-Act, the Federal Government vide S.R.O.
1647(I)/2025 dated 28.08.2025 has notified the NCCIA as
the investigating and prosecuting agency under the
Page-6
ICAs No.359, 360, 361 & 362 of 2025
referred Act. Furthermore, in exercised of the powers
conferred by section 42 of the 2010-Act, the Federal
Government through S.R.O. 1648(I)/2025, dated
28.08.2025 inserted section XV – Prevention of Electronic
Crimes Act, 2016 in Schedule-I to section 2(xxvi) of the
2010-Act which includes the offences under sections 10,
14, 16, 17, 22, 22A, 22B, 22C and 26A of the 2016-Act.
12. Section 2(xxiii) of the 2010-Act defines the
‗offence of money laundering‘ as the same offence defined
in section 3 thereof. The expression ‗proceeds of crime‘
has been defined in clause (xxvii) of section 2 as meaning
any property derived or obtained directly or indirectly by
any person from the commission of a predicate offence or
foreign serious offence. The term ‗predicate offence‘ has
been defined in clause (xxvi) of section 2 as meaning the
offences specified in Schedule-I to the 2010-Act. Section 3
of the 2010-Act provides that a person shall be guilty of
the offence of money laundering, if (i) he acquires,
converts, possesses, uses or transfers property, knowing
or having reason to believe that such property is proceeds
of crime; (ii) conceals or disguises the true nature, origin,
location, disposition, movement or ownership of property,
knowing or having reason to believe that such property is
proceeds of crime; (iii) holds or possesses on behalf of
any other person any property knowing or having reason
to believe that such property is proceeds of crime and (iv)
participates in, associates, conspires or commit, attempts
to commit, aids, abets, facilitates, or counsels the
commission of the referred acts.
13. In terms of section 8 of the 2010-Act, the
investigating officer/prosecution agency, with the approval
of the “Court”, can provisionally attach the property
Page-7
ICAs No.359, 360, 361 & 362 of 2025
“involved” in money laundering for a period not exceeding
one hundred and eighty days from the date of the order.
This period, however, can further be extended for a period
of one hundred and eighty days. Sub section (3) of section
8 of the 2010-Act provides that the attachment order
passed by the investigating officer shall seize to have
effect on expiry of the stipulated period or the time,
subject to sub-sections (2) & (3) of section 9 of the 2010-
Act. Under section 9(2) if the investigating
officer/prosecution agency determines during the
investigations that the properties provisionally attached
are involved in money laundering, then he shall apply to
the Court under section 9(3) of the Act of 2010 for
confirmation of the attachment till conclusion of the trial.
The expression „Court‟ has been defined as Court specified
under section 20 of the 2010-Act i.e. the Court of
Sessions.
14. Unlike the provisions of 2010-Act and the
1974-Act, the provisions of 2016-Act do not expressly
empower the NCCIA to attach, caution or freeze properties
of citizens, pending inquiries/investigations. The NCCIA
appears to have assumed this power pursuant to rule 5 of
the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (Function)
Rules, 2025 (hereinafter the ‗Rules‘) framed in exercise of
powers conferred by section 51 of the 2016-Act read with
sections 27 and 29 thereof, notified vide S.R.O
1639(I)/2025 published in the official gazette on
28.08.2025. For the sake of convenience, rule 5 of Rules
is reproduced below.-
―5. Powers of the members of the
NCCIA.—(1) The NCCIA conducting an inquiry or
investigation may freeze a property, directly
connected to commission of an offence under the
Act.
Page-8
ICAs No.359, 360, 361 & 362 of 2025
(2) Prior permission shall be obtained
from the authorized officer as designated by the
Director General before freezing or de-freezing of
the property.
(3) Any contravention of order made
under sub-rule (2) shall be punishable under
section 174 or 188 of Pakistan Penal Code (Act
XLV of 1860).‖
15. Bare perusal of sections 27 of 2016-Act shows
that the same deals with legal recognition of offences
committed in relation to information system. Likewise,
section 28 relates to application of provisions of Pakistan
Penal Code, 1860 to the offence provided in the 2010-Act.
Section 52 of the 2016-Act, however, empowers the
Federal Government to make rules for carrying out
purpose of the Act, including the subjects mentioned in
sub-section (2) thereof, which is reproduced below.-
―51. Power to make rules.— (1) The Federal
Government may, by notification in the official
Gazette, make rules for carrying out purposes of
this Act.
(2) Without prejudice to the generality of
the foregoing powers, such rules may specify,—
(a) qualifications and trainings of the officers
and staff of the investigation agency and
prosecutors;
(b) powers, functions and responsibilities of
the investigation agency, its officers and
prosecutors;
(c) standard, operating procedures of the
investigation agency;
(d) mode and manner in which record of
investigation under this Act may be
maintained;
(e) manner to deal with the seized data,
information system, device or other
articles;
(f) working of joint investigation teams;
(g) requirements for seeking permission of
the Authority to change, alter or re-
programme unique device identifier of
any communication equipment by any
person for research or any other
legitimate purpose;
Page-9
ICAs No.359, 360, 361 & 362 of 2025
(h) procedure for seeking appropriate order
of the Authority for removal, or blocking
of online content;
(i) constitution of computer emergency
response team and the standard
operating procedure to be adopted by
such team;
(j) appointment of designated agency
having capability to collect real time
information;
(k) manner of coordination between the
investigation agency and other law
enforcement and intelligence agencies
including designated agency;
(l) for management and oversight of the
forensic laboratory;
(m) qualifications and trainings of the
officers, experts and staff of the forensic
laboratory;
(n) powers, functions and responsibilities of
the forensic laboratory, its officers,
experts and staff;
(o) standard operating procedures of the
forensic laboratory to interact with the
investigation agency;
(p) manner of soliciting and extending
international cooperation;
(q) matters connected or ancillary thereto;
and
(r) provision of fines for contravention of the
provisions of this Act and rules made
thereunder.‖
16. It is highlighted here that the collection and
preservation of data/evidence relating to the commission
of offences under the 2016-Act is different from freezing
of the properties i.e. Bank accounts of persons, for which
express sanction of the Legislature in the parent statute
i.e. 2016-Act is required. There is plethora of judgments
1
that subordinate legislation shall neither be in conflict with
1
Mian Zaiuddin v. Punjab Local Government and others [1985 SCMR 365],
Khawaja Ahmed Hassan v. Government of Punjab and others [2005 SCMR
186], Suo Motu Case No.11/2011, in the matter of National Police Foundation
Land [PLD 2014 SC 389], Suo Motu Case No.13/2009 [PLD 2011 SC 619],
Zarai Taraqiati Bank Limited and others v. Said Rehman and others [2013
SCMR 642], Farrukh Raza Sheikh v. The Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue
and others [2022 SCMR 1787], Khawaja Ahmad Hassan v. Government of
Punjab and others [2005 SCMR 186].
Page-10
ICAs No.359, 360, 361 & 362 of 2025
the provisions of parent statute nor travel beyond its
permissible scope and that the rule making authority shall
not act as Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) to assume powers
not delegated by the parent law. Rules 5 of the Rules
thus appears to have been framed in excess of the powers
delegated by sections 27, 28 and 51 of the 2016-Act.
17. The NCCIA appears to have diverted the
process prescribed under the 2010-Act. In case, the
NCCIA was of the view that the amounts available in the
Bank accounts of the appellants were the proceeds of
crime (as defined section 2(xxvii) of 2010-Act) or derived
out of the predicate offences (as provided in section XV of
Schedule-I to section 2(xxvi) of the 2010-Act) then the
proper course was to obtain an order of the Court in terms
of section 8 of the 2010-Act.
18. The inquiry was initiated by the NCCIA on the
basis of its own source report, which did not bifurcated the
roles of each appellant in the commission of alleged
offences, if any. In fact, a detailed inquiry was required to
be conducted by associating the appellants in the process,
disclosing the allegations on the basis whereof the NCCIA
initiated criminal proceedings under the 2016-Act.
Instead, the NCCIA proceeded in haste and directly
approached the concerned Banks for freezing of the Bank
accounts of appellants, which may affect their rights to
property, livelihood and life guaranteed under the
Constitution. Further, the nature of allegations required
detailed probe and it is for the trial court, if a criminal
case is subsequently filed, to strike a balance between the
right of appellants protected Article 19 of the Constitution
and the provisions of the 2016-Act. In the attending
circumstances, we conclude that the impugned action of
Page-11
ICAs No.359, 360, 361 & 362 of 2025
NCCIA whereby the Bank accounts of appellants were
blocked on the basis of its own source report was
disproportionate, harsh and unreasonable, particularly to
the extent of family members of persons regarding whom
the allegations were leveled. The impugned judgment is,
therefore, liable to be set-aside.
19. For what has been discussed above, the Intra
Court Appeals are allowed. Consequently, the impugned
judgment is hereby set-aside. The respondents are
directed to unfreeze/unblock the Bank accounts of the
appellants forthwith. The NCCIA is directed to proceed
with the inquiry strictly in accordance with law.
(INAAM AMEEN MINHAS) (ARBAB MUHAMMAD TAHIR)
JUDGE JUDGE
Announced in the open Court on .10.2025.
JUDGE JUDGE
Approved for reporting.
Luqman Khan/*
