before: Honourable Mr. Justice Muhammad Azam Khan
author: Honourable Mr. Justice Muhammad Azam Khan
description: Agaisnt placement of name on ECL.
discussed_laws: under Article 199, 2A, 4, 9, 10A, 15, and 25of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973 | under Sections 20, 21, and 24 of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016.
judgment_link: https://mis.ihc.gov.pk/frmRdJgmnt.aspx?cseNo=Writ Petition-2935-2025 | -&cseTle=RABIA BASRI VS FOP&jgs=Honourable Mr. Justice Muhammad Azam Khan&jgmnt=/attachments/judgements/201120/1/201120_638968948347636756.pdf
pdf_data:
JUDGMENT SHEET
IN THE ISLAMABAD HIGH COURT,
ISLAMABAD
W.P. NO. 2935 OF 2025
RABIA BASRI
Vs.
FEDERATION OF PAKISTAN THROUGH THE
SECRETARY, MINISTRY OF INTERIOR, ETC.
Petitioner by : Ms. Laraib Kanwal, Advocate.
Respondents by : Raja M. Saeed, D.A.G.
Pir Sohail, A.D. Legal, and Mr. Muhammad
Saleem, A.D. Passport.
Date of hearing : 13.10.2025
MUHAMMAD AZAM KHAN, J.
1. Through the instant Writ Petition filed under Article 199 of the
Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as
the “Constitution”), Rabia Basri (“Petitioner”) seeks declaration to the effect
that act of the Respondents in blocking of her Passport/placing her name of Exit
Control List (ECL) is illegal, unlawful, violative of fundamental rights
guaranteed by the Constitution, without lawful authority and of no legal effect.
The Petitioner also seeks directions to the respondents to unblock her passport
forthwith.
2. Brief facts of the case, as per the contents of the petition, are that the
Petitioner has been residing abroad on the basis of a residency visa, which is due
to expire in November 2025. In order to comply with immigration regulations
and to extend her legal stay, she visited the Pakistan Consulate Office for the
purpose of applying for a visa extension. She was informed that her passport had
been blocked pursuant to the directions issued by the Federal Investigation
Agency (F.I.A.). Being aggrieved, the Petitioner has filed the instant petition.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner contends that the impugned actions of
the respondents have caused the petitioner severe hardship, infringing upon her
fundamental rights to liberty, due process, and freedom of movement, as
guaranteed under Articles 2A, 4, 9, 10A, 15, and 25 of the Constitution of the
2
W.P. No. 2935/2025
Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973. The petitioner has learned through reliable
sources that multiple FIRs have been maliciously registered against her by her
former husband and/or his relatives with the sole intent to harass, defame, and
humiliate her. She was neither properly served nor given any opportunity to be
heard before her passport was blocked and her name placed on the Provisional
Control List (PCL), in clear violation of due process and principles of natural
justice. The blocking of the petitioner’s passport was carried out without the
issuance of a Show Cause Notice or a speaking order, as required under Rule 23
of the Passport Rules, 2021, Section 8(2) of the Passport Act, 1974, and Section
24A of the General Clauses Act, 1897. These legal provisions mandate that any
such executive action must be reasonable, lawful, and preceded by an
opportunity to be heard. The petitioner is a Pakistani citizen with no prior
criminal record. She currently resides in Dubai for personal safety, and due to
the blocking of her passport, she is unable to renew her residence visa, which is
valid only until November 2025. This places her at imminent risk of deportation
and potential statelessness. The placement of her name on the ECL also suffers
from legal infirmities, having been done without due process, lawful
justification, or consideration of proportionality. There is no conviction or legal
ground under the relevant laws to justify such restrictions. The petitioner’s case
does not fall under any of the exceptions listed in Rule 23 of the Passport Rules,
2021, or Section 8 of the Passport Act, 1974, which allow for cancellation or
impounding of a passport only under specific, legally-defined circumstances
such as fraud, national security, or being a proclaimed offender. The actions of
the respondents are arbitrary, excessive, malafide, and ultra vires the
Constitution. They violate her dignity, liberty, and the right to travel, and are
without jurisdiction or lawful authority. Lastly, learned counsel prayed for
immediate directions for the unblocking of her passport and removal of her
name from the PCL/ECL to prevent further unlawful hardship, and to safeguard
her fundamental rights.
4. On behalf of Respondents No.1 to 3, it is submitted that name of the
Petitioner was placed on “Passport Control List (PCL)” on 13.09.2023, as per
3
W.P. No. 2935/2025
provisions contained in Rules 21 & 22 (2)(b) of the Passport Rules, 2021, on the
recommendation of the FIA, being involved in case FIR No.105/2023 of FIA
CCRC, Islamabad.
5. On behalf of F.I.A., a report is submitted according to which a case u/s
20, 21, 24 PECA, 2016 r/w 109, 34 PPC is registered against the
Petitioner/Accused. During the investigation of the said case, a request was
made to the competent court on 24.07.2023 to order for placement of the
accused petitioner on the Passport Control List, under Passport Rules, 2021.
Accordingly, the accused was placed on the PCL of Immigration and Passport.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned D.A.G., and
perused the record with their able assistance.
7. The petitioner, Rabia Basri, through the instant writ petition under Article
199 of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973, seeks
declaratory relief against the alleged unlawful and arbitrary actions of the
respondents in blocking her passport and placing her name on the Exit Control
List (ECL) and/or Passport Control List (PCL). The petitioner contends that
these actions are violative of her constitutionally guaranteed fundamental rights,
particularly those enshrined under Articles 4, 9, 10A, 15, and 25 of the
Constitution. It is further claimed that these measures were taken without
issuance of a show cause notice or affording her an opportunity of hearing, in
contravention of Rule 23 of the Passport Rules, 2021, Section 8(2) of the
Passport Act, 1974, and Section 24A of the General Clauses Act, 1897, which
collectively mandate that any adverse executive action be preceded by reasons
recorded in writing and a right to be heard.
8. As per the factual matrix emerging from the record, the petitioner has
been residing abroad and currently holds a valid residency visa which, as per her
own contention, is set to expire in November 2025. She approached the Pakistan
Consulate seeking a visa extension and was then informed that her passport had
been blocked pursuant to directions issued by the Federal Investigation Agency
4
W.P. No. 2935/2025
(FIA). The petitioner alleges that she has learned through "reliable sources" that
multiple FIRs have been lodged against her by her former husband or his
associates, purportedly to malign her and cause her harassment. However, these
allegations, being unsubstantiated and uncorroborated by documentary evidence,
cannot be examined in writ jurisdiction without a proper factual inquiry.
9. The respondents, on the other hand, have submitted their replies supported
by the relevant record. It is confirmed that the name of the petitioner was placed
on the PCL on 13.09.2023 pursuant to a request initiated by the Federal
Investigation Agency (FIA) during the investigation of FIR No. 105/2023,
registered at the FIA Cyber Crime Reporting Centre, Islamabad. The FIR alleges
commission of offences under Sections 20, 21, and 24 of the Prevention of
Electronic Crimes Act, 2016, read with Sections 109 and 34 of the Pakistan
Penal Code. The request for inclusion of the petitioner’s name in the PCL was
made, and her name was placed on the PCL as per provisions contained in Rules
21 & 22(2)(b) of the Passport Rules, 2021.
10. Significantly, it has been confirmed by the FIA that the petitioner
was declared a Proclaimed Offender by the trial court concerned after failing to
join the investigation or appear before the court despite the issuance of due
process notices and warrants. The proclamation proceedings were initiated in
accordance with the provisions of Section 87 Cr.P.C., and the declaration as a
Proclaimed Offender has not been challenged or set aside by the petitioner to
date. Once a person has been declared a Proclaimed Offender, she ceases to
enjoy the same standing before a constitutional court as an ordinary litigant. It is
now settled law that a person who is deliberately avoiding the process of law
and absconding from judicial proceedings cannot invoke the extraordinary
constitutional jurisdiction of the High Court for the enforcement of her
fundamental rights, while simultaneously continuing to disregard lawful judicial
orders. The right to seek equitable relief, particularly under Article 199, is
subject to the petitioner approaching the court with clean hands and in
compliance with the rule of law. A proclaimed offender, by virtue of the
5
W.P. No. 2935/2025
declaration, is deemed to be evading justice and, thus, disentitled to
discretionary relief unless she first submits herself to the jurisdiction of the court
that issued the proclamation.
11. Moreover, the petitioner’s argument that the blocking of her passport and
inclusion on the PCL were undertaken without notice or opportunity of hearing
must be viewed in light of her own absence from the jurisdiction and her
continued non-cooperation in the criminal investigation. Where a person is
absconding and has been formally declared as a proclaimed offender, issuance
of show cause notices or pre-decisional hearings becomes impracticable and, in
certain situations, legally unnecessary. Executive actions taken under judicial
direction, or pursuant to criminal proceedings, are afforded a presumption of
regularity, particularly where the subject has been evading process.
12. The petitioner’s claim of being at risk of deportation from the host
country due to the non-renewal of her residency visa, while unfortunate, cannot
override the legal obligation she has to submit to the judicial process in Pakistan.
She retains the right to travel back to Pakistan through Emergency Travel
Documents, which may be obtained from the Pakistan Mission abroad. Upon her
return, she may surrender before the trial court, explain her absence, and move
for cancellation of the proclamation order. Subject to the trial court’s
satisfaction, she may also seek appropriate relief, including the unblocking of
her passport and removal of her name from the PCL or ECL.
13. In light of the foregoing, it is apparent that the impugned actions of the
respondents were not arbitrary, unlawful, or without jurisdiction, but were taken
pursuant to legal provisions and in furtherance of judicial proceedings. No
malafide or extraneous motives have been demonstrated by the petitioner.
Resultantly, the instant petition is dismissed being devoid of any merits.
(MUHAMMAD AZAM KHAN)
JUDGE

Form No: HCJD/C-121
ORDER SHEET
IN THE ISLAMABAD HIGH COURT, ISLAMABAD
(JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT)
I.C.A. No.437/2019
Muhammad Ishaq Khan and others
Versus
Federation of Pakistan,
Ministry of Interior through its Secretary and others
I.C.A. No.438/2019
Mehmood-ul-Hassan and others
Versus
Shafqat Jamal, Inspector and others
Appellants by : Mr Shah Khawar, Advocate.
Mr Muhammad Munir Paracha,A Advocate.
Mr Ali Nawaz Kharral, Advocate.
Respondents by : Mr Sultan Lehrasib Khan, Asstt. Attorney
General.
Date of Hearing : 11.09.2025
Arbab Muhammad Tahir, J- Through the
titled appeals in terms of section 3(2) of the Law Reforms
Ordinance, 1972, the appellants have assailed order, dated
01.11.2019, passed by the learned Single Judge whereby W. P.
No.2871/2013 filed by private respondents, was disposed of.
For the sake of convenience, the impugned order is reproduced
as follows.-
“After hearing the parties at some length, it
appears that the petitioners have assailed the
appointments of respondents No.6 to 80, who
have been appointed in the FIA on different
positions in BPS 16, 17, & 18, in a project,
however, in the light of judgment rendered by
Division Bench of this Court in ICA No.340/2017
titled (Imran Ahmed & another Vs. Federation of
Pakistan, etc.) and Writ petition No.4837/2018
Page:2:
ICAs No. 437 & 438 of 2019
titled (Nadeem Akhter Vs. FOP, etc.), all the said
respondents could not be considered as civil
servants, unless their credentials, experience and
eligibility have been considered under FIA
Appointment, Promotion and Transfer (APT),
Rules, 1975 r/w Federal Public Service Rules and
Ordinance, 1977, which makes it mandatory that
posts of BPS-16 and above could only be filled
through a competitive process.
2. The Additional Director (Law), FIA as well
as learned Assistant Attorney General has been
confronted to that effect, whereupon, they
requested that case of respondents No.6 to 80
will be transmitted to FPSC in light of judgment
passed by the Hon‟ble Division Bench of this
Court in I.C.A. No.340/2017 titled (Imran Ahmed
& others Vs. Federation of Pakistan, etc.)
reported as 2019 PLC(CS) N 19 Islamabad.
3. Keeping in view the above, Director General
FIA and Secretary, Ministry of Interior are
directed to transmit the case of respondents No.6
to 80 to the Federal Public Service Commission,
who shall consider their eligibility, educational
record and other relevant credentials in terms of
Section 11(b) of Civil Servant Act, 1973 r/w
powers conferred in Rules 4 & 5 of the FPSC
(function), Rules, 1978.
4. Instant writ petition stands disposed of, in
view of above terms. However, it is expected
from the Federal Public Service Commission,
Islamabad to decide the question of eligibility or
otherwise of respondents No.6 to 80 within six
(06) months from the date of receiving of record
from the Director General, FIA and Secretary,
Ministry of Interior.”
2. The facts relevant for adjudication of the titled
appeals are that the appellants and private respondents
are/were serving in the Federal Investigation Agency
(hereinafter „Agency‟). The appellants in ICA No.437/2019 were
initially employed by the Agency in its project titled Personal
Identification, Secure Comparison and Evaluation System
(hereinafter „PICES-Project‟) since 2002 and onwards. In 2010,
124 posts of the PICES-Project were converted from
development to non-development side. Whereas, the appellants
in ICA No.438/2019 were initially appointed by the Agency in
Page:3:
ICAs No. 437 & 438 of 2019
the project titled National Response Centre for Cyber Crimes
(hereinafter „NR3C-Project‟). In 2012, 83 posts of the NR3C-
Project were converted from development to non-development
side. Needless to mention that all the appellants were appointed
after adopting transparent competitive process by the Agency.
The cases of employees of the above referred projects were
subsequently considered by the Cabinet Sub-Committee for
Regularization of Contract Employees and were ultimately
recommended to be regularized in the year 2012/2013. The
Agency while acting upon the recommendations of the Cabinet
Sub-Committee ordered regularization of the appellants. A writ
of quo warranto was filed against the appellants by three of
their colleagues i.e. Shafqat Jamal Inspector, Tahir Khan,
Inspector and Naeem Iqbal, Sub Inspector, which was disposed
of by the learned Single Judge through the impugned order
reproduced above, hence these appeals.
3. Learned counsel for the appellants have argued that
the impugned order is non-speaking; that it lacks the
determination of the question of law raised by the petitioner in
the writ petition; that the learned Single Judge was obligated to
look into the bonafides of the writ petitioners and to see as to
whether the documents annexed with the writ petition were
lawfully obtained; that the case of the appellants were declared
as past and closed transaction by a learned Division Bench of
this Court in paragraph 123(ix) judgment titled „Imran Ahmed &
others Vs. Federation of Pakistan, etc‟ (2019 PLC(CS)N 19
Islamabad); that the learned Single Judge did not afford
adequate opportunity to the appellants to plead their case; that
the writ petition was decided in a summary manner by
misapplication of the principles and law enunciated in Imran
Ahmed‟s case; that under the referred principles, only the cases
of those employees who were not regularized at the time of
passing of the referred judgment could be sent to the Federal
Page:4:
ICAs No. 437 & 438 of 2019
Public Service Commission; that the case of the appellants was
grossly misunderstood; that the appellants had already been
regularized prior to pronouncement of the judgment in Imran
Ahmed‟s case; that the learned Single Judge wrongly assumed
that the case of the appellants fall within paragraph 123(iii) of
the judgment in Imran Ahmed‟s case; that appellants were
appointed through a transparent competitive process; that their
service rules were accordingly amended; that in case of
employees of the Cyber Crimes Wing of the Agency, they now
stand transferred to the NCCIA by virtue of section 29(5) of the
2016-Act; that the impugned judgment is liable to be set-aside.
4. Conversely, learned Assistant Attorney General
argued that the impugned order is well reasoned; the learned
Single Judge afforded sufficient opportunity of hearing to the
parties; that the appointment of the appellants was not in
accordance with law; that the principles and law enunciated in
Imran Ahmed‟s case, supra, particularly paragraph 123(iii)
thereof attracted and was duly applied by the learned Single
Judge while passing the impugned order; that the case of
appellants does not fall within the ambit of the past and closed
transaction; that amendment in the service rules cannot remedy
inherent lapses in the appointment of the appellants; that after
conversion of the posts held by appellants from development to
non-development side, the same were required to be advertised
and filled through open competitive process in accordance with
law; that the regularization of the appellants was not made in
accordance with law; the case does not fall within the category
of past and close transaction in light of the judgment titled
“Mohsin Raza Gondal and others v. Sardar Mahmood and
others” (2025 SCMR 104); that the instant appeal is liable to be
dismissed.
5. Heard. Record perused.
Page:5:
ICAs No. 437 & 438 of 2019
6. Perusal of the impugned order (reproduced in
paragraph 1) above shows that the learned Single Judge did not
advert to the merits of the case by duly formulating the points
for determination and recording findings after hearing
contentions of the parties, rather the writ petition was
summarily decided relying upon the principles and law
enunciated by a learned Division Bench of this Court in Imran
Ahmed‟s case, supra. The question before us is, whether the
learned Single Judge while passing the impugned order correctly
categorized the case of the appellants in light of Imran Ahmed‟s
case, supra?
7. Before responding to the above question, it is
essential to go through the statutory scheme dealing with the
appellants‟ (incumbents) merger alongwith posts in the Agency.
There is no denial to the fact that the services of appellants
were regularized in 2012/2013. After conversion of the PICES
and NR3C projects from the development to non-development
side, the Ministry of Interior, in exercise of powers conferred by
sub rule (2) of Rule 3 of the Civil Servants (Appointment,
Promotion & Transfer) Rules, 1973 and Section 7(1)(b)(i) & (ii)
of Federal Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1977, issued
notification S.R.O. 1(KE)/2015, dated 23.09.2014, published in
the official gazette on 02.01.2015 (hereinafter the „FIA Rules‟)
whereby the method, qualifications and other conditions for
appointment to posts in various pay scales upto BPS-21 in the
Federal Investigation Agency were laid down. Rule 3 of the FIA
Rules deals with the conditions for promotion of various cadres
and posts in different Groups in the Agency. The Proviso (a) to
Rule 3 of the FIA Rules is relevant to the case of the appellants,
which reads as follows.-
“a) The incumbents working in Customs,
Income Tax & Engineering Groups shall be
merged alongwith posts they are occupying
in “investigation Group” against the post(s)
Page:6:
ICAs No. 437 & 438 of 2019
of equivalent grade/scale. The Forensic and
Information Technology Experts working in
Technical Wing, CTW, NR3C, the erstwhile
PICES and IBMS shall be merged alongwith
post(s) of equivalent grade/scale. This will
be one time dispensation. Further the
incumbents working in the sub groups of
Forensic Expert Group like CTW, NR3C,
IBMS, etc. shall be posted only in the areas
of their expertise.”
(underlined to add emphasis)
8. It is thus clear from the Proviso (a) to Rule 3 of
the FIA Rules that appellants (incumbents) were merged
alongwith posts in the Agency by virtue of a statutory
provision, as a one-time dispensation. This extra ordinary
dispensation was particularly given to the appellants after
obtaining concurrence of the (i) Establishment Division and,
(ii) Federal Public Service Commission, as reflected in Rule 7
ibid, which is reproduced below.-
“7. This Notification issues with the
concurrence of the Establishment Division vide
their O.M. No. 12/3/89-R5, dated 4th July, 2014
and FPSC vide its Letter No.F.15-14/2013-RR,
dated 23rd September, 2014.”
It goes without saying that the concurrence of the
Federal Public Service Commission was in pursuance of its
powers conferred by section 11B of the Civil Servants Act, 1973.
9. In addition, by virtue of section 6 of the Prevention
of Electronic Crimes (Amendment) Act, 2025, section 29 of the
Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016 (hereinafter the
„2016-Act‟), was substituted. Section 29(1) whereof provides
that the Federal Government shall establish an investigation
agency to be called the National Cyber Crimes Investigation
Agency (NCCIA). Section 29(5) of the 2016-Act further provides
that after establishment of the NCCIA, the Cyber Crimes Wing
of the Federal Investigation Agency shall cease to exist and all
Page:7:
ICAs No. 437 & 438 of 2019
personnel, cases, inquiries, investigations, assets, properties,
budget, liabilities, rights, obligations, privileges and matters
related thereto or connected therewith in respect of the defunct
Cyber Crimes Wing of the Agency shall stand transferred to the
NCCIA. In pursuance of section 29(5), the Federal Government
vide S.R.O. 748(I)/2025, has duly established the NCCIA of
investigation of the offences under the 2016-Act. Thus, all the
matters relating to the defunct Cyber Crimes Wing of the
Agency including the personnel employed therein now stand
transferred to the NCCIA by virtue of a statutory provision. This
is substantial change in the legislative framework relating to the
appellants in ICA No.438/2019.
10. Adverting to the question framed above, the cases
seeking regularization of contract/daily wages employments
came before this Court in various petitions. The said petitions
were decided vide consolidated judgment reported as 2018 PLC
(CS) 619 titled „Shagufta Hashmat v. Federation of Pakistan,
through Secretary Cabinet Division, etc.‟ In the referred
judgment, this Court had discussed in detail the concept of
initial appointment and the petitions filed by individuals seeking
regularization of their services were remitted to the concerned
competent authority for consideration under the new policy. The
referred judgment was later assailed through various Intra
Court Appeals before this Court, which were decided vide
consolidated judgment in the Imran Ahmed‟s case supra. The
learned Division Bench of this Court upheld the judgment in
Shagufta Hashmat‟s case, but with additional directions in
paragraph 123 thereof.
11. It is noteworthy that in Imran‟s Ahmed case, the
learned Division Bench had made it clear that all project
employees who are appointed in BPS-16 and above in a
transparent manner, “but could not claim regularization of their
services” were to be referred to the FPSC for determination of
Page:8:
ICAs No. 437 & 438 of 2019
their eligibility. For the sake of convenience paragraph 123(iii)
of the referred judgment is reproduced below.-
“All project employees who are appointed in
BPS-16 and above on project could not claim
regularization of their services unless their
projects have been converted from development
to non-development phase by the Government of
Pakistan. In such eventuality, all those employees
who are working on those projects shall continue
to work and if their initial appointments in the
project have been made through a transparent
manner i.e. advertisement, test, and interview,
then their cases be sent to FPSC in terms of
Section 11(b) of the Civil Servants Act, 1973 read
with the powers referred in Rule 4 & 5 of the
FPSC (Functions) Rules, 1978. Their posts and
their appointments shall be considered
regularized subject to decision of the FPSC on the
question of their eligibility, qualification and
fitness merely on the basis of opinion of FPSC or
conducting test and interview within a period of
six Months.”
(underlined to add emphasis)
It was further directed in clause (ix) of
paragraph 123 of Imran Ahmed‟s case, supra as follows.-
“(ix) Employees who are already working in
different Ministries, Divisions, etc. whose their
services have been regularized; they should not
be disturbed as their cases fall within the ambit of
past and closed transaction, subject to conditions
that they were appointed in accordance with law
in a transparent manner.”
(highlighted to add emphasis)
12. At the time, when the impugned judgment was
passed by the learned Single Judge, the judgment in Imran
Ahmed‟s case, supra, was already in the field, rendered by a
learned Division Bench of this Court. The judgment in Imran
Ahmed‟s case supra was subsequently upheld by the Hon‟ble
Supreme Court vide judgment, dated 13-03-2019, passed in
C.P. No.2792/2018, titled „Muhammad Imran Khan v.
Federation of Pakistan thr. Secretary to the Government of
Page:9:
ICAs No. 437 & 438 of 2019
Pakistan M/o Information Technology and Telecom Division,
Islamabad & others. The regularization of the appellants is
protected by paragraph 123(ix) of Imran Ahmed‟s case, supra.
13. The impugned order has been based by the learned
Single Judge on paragraph 123(iii) of the Imran Ahmed‟s case.
The learned Single Judge while passing the impugned order; did
not appreciate the points, (i) the appellants were not before the
learned Single Judge seeking regularization of their services,
(ii) that their services had already been regularized in the year
2013 and thus the protection in paragraph 123(ix) of Imran
Ahmed‟s case was attracted and that (iii) applicable service
rules were suitably amended by merging the appellants
(incumbents) in the Agency through grant of “one time
dispensation” in consultation with Federal Public Service
Commission. Furthermore, the impugned order cannot be
treated as a speaking order as it fails to formulate the questions
of law for determination and recording of conclusive findings in
light of the contentions of the parties. It appears that the
impugned order was passed in haste. The petition before the
learned Single Judge was in the nature of quo warranto which
essentially obligated the Court to look into the bonafides of the
relator and the mode of acquisition of official record annexed
with the petition by the writ petitioner.
14. The Hon‟ble Supreme Court in the case titled “Dr
Azim-Ur-Rehman Khan Meo v. Government of Sind and
another” (2004 SCMR 1294) has held that “…writ jurisdiction
irrespective of its kind, is discretionary which is required to be
exercised judiciously but the High Court would be fully
competent while exercising such discretion to test the bona
fides of the relator to see if he has come with clean hands. In
this regard reference can be made to Federation of Pakistan v.
Muhammad Saifullah Khan PLD 1989 SC 166 and Federation of
Pakistan v. Muhammad Saifullah Khan 1989 SCMR 1996. In
Page:10:
ICAs No. 437 & 438 of 2019
case it is determined that the appellant had approached the
Court with ulterior motive, mala fide intention and as an
instrument of others, the relief can be declined. If any authority
is needed reliance can be placed on A.M. Khan Leghari v.
Government of Pakistan PLD 1967 La&. 227 (1711)”. In the
case of Dr Azim-Ur-Rehman Khan Meo, supra, the Hon‟ble
Supreme Court further observed that procuring official record
through unlawful means is a classic example of misuse and
abuse of authority which must not escape unnoticed. Such an
act by a Government servant was held to be breach of trust and
violation of Government Servants (Conduct Rules). In the
referred case, the Hon‟ble Supreme Court issued direction to the
employer to initiate disciplinary action against the litigant who
was a Government Servant.
15. The learned Assistant Attorney General has placed
reliance on the judgment rendered by the Hon‟ble Supreme
Court in Mohsin Raza Gondal‟s case, supra. The referred
judgment is distinguishable in the facts and circumstances of
the instant case. First, the applicable service rules were suitably
amended by granting one time dispensation, which are in force
with full legal validity; second, the learned Single Judge has
wrongly categorized the appellants in clause (iii) of paragraph
123 of the judgment in Imran Ahmed‟s case instead of clause
(ix) thereof, and secondly, the regularization of the appellants
followed by the protection in Imran Ahmed‟s case, supra, has
created rights in their favour. Such rights can, therefore, not be
disturbed by giving retrospective application to the judgment in
Mohsin Raza Gondal‟s case. The Hon‟ble Supreme Court in the
case titled “Zarai Taraqiati Bank Limited through President and
others v. Sarfraz Khan Jadoon and others” (2021 SCMR 1305)
held that “…it is an established legal principle of law that the
judgments of the Courts always operate prospectively. In this
regard reliance can well be placed on the case of Pakistan
Page:11:
ICAs No. 437 & 438 of 2019
Medical and Dental Council through President and 3 others v.
Muhammad Fahad Malik and 10 others (2018 SCMR 1956)
and the case Regarding Pensionary Benefits of the Judges of
Superior Courts from the date of their Respective
Retirements, Irrespective of their length of Service as Such
Judges (PLD 2013 SC 829).”
16. In the case titled “Rao Abdul Rehman (Deceased)
through legal heirs v. Muhammad Afzal (Deceased) through
legal heirs and others” (2023 SCMR 815), it has been held that
“According to the dictum laid down in the case of Pakistan
Medical and Dental Council and others v. Muhammad Fahad
Malik and others (2018 SCMR 1956) the judgments of this
Court (Supreme Court) unless declared otherwise operate
prospectively. More or less, similar findings that the law laid
down by this Court is prospective which cannot be doubted
have been recorded in the case of Sakhi Muhammad and
another v. Capital Development Authority, Islamabad (PLD
1991 SC 777) and Pir Bakhsh and others v. The Chairman,
Allotment Committee and others (PLD 1987 SC 145).”
17. In the case titled “Pir Bakhsh represented by his
Legal Heirs and others v. The Chairman, Allotment Committee
and others” (PLD 1987 SC 145) “So, long this determination
was not set aside in appeal, the judgment remained in the field
irrespective of the quality of determination as to whether it was
incorrect on questions of fact or law. The rights of the parties
thereunder assumed finality and took the colour of a "past and
closed transaction." The fact that the Supreme Court in an
appeal, titled Abdul Hafiz v. Rehabilitation Commissioner and
others, against the judgment of the High Court set aside the
same judgment in another writ petition would not reopen the
concluded rights of the parties under the decision of the High
Courts against which no appeal was filed nor could the
appellants who were respondents in that writ petition avail the
Page:12:
ICAs No. 437 & 438 of 2019
benefit of the law laid down by the Supreme Court under Article
189 of the Constitution.”
18. In view of the above, it is concluded that the
learned Single Judge failed to consider Proviso (a) to Rule 3 of
the FIA Rules, by virtue of which the appellants (incumbents)
were merged alongwith posts in the Agency, which merger was
with the concurrence of the Establishment Division as well as
Federal Public Service Commission as reflected in Rule 7 of the
FIA Rules. Furthermore, the learned Single Judge failed to apply
correctly the principles and law enunciated in Imran Ahmed‟s
case, supra, as the appellants were wrongly categorized in
clause (iii) of paragraph 123 of the judgment instead of clause
(ix) thereof, which judgment had attained finality upto the
Hon‟ble Supreme Court. In addition, the impugned order being
adverse to the appellants, fails to demonstrate adjudication and
determination of rights by appreciating their contentions and
material placed on record. The impugned order is, therefore,
legally not sustainable and liable to be set-aside.
19. For what has been discussed above, the titled
appeals i.e. ICA No.437 & 438 of 2019 are allowed.
Consequently, the impugned order, dated 01.11.2019, passed
by the learned Single Judge in W.P. No.2871 of 2013, is hereby
set-aside. Parties are left to bear their own costs.
(INAAM AMEEN MINHAS) (ARBAB MUHAMMAD TAHIR)
JUDGE JUDGE
Announced in the open Court on .10.2025.
JUDGE JUDGE
Luqman Khan/*

ORDER SHEET
IN THE ISLAMABAD HIGH COURT, ISLAMABAD.
JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT.
Crl. Misc. No.1468-B-2025
Raja Muhammad Adil
Versus
The State and another.
S. No. of Date of Order with signature of Judge and that of parties or
order/ order/ counsel where necessary.
proceedings Proceedings
(05) 02.10.2025 Mr. Asif Ali Tamboli, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. Shahid Shabbir, Advocate for Complainant.
Mr. Usman Rasool Ghumman, AAG.
Asif Nawaz, Deputy Director, F.I.A, CCRC,
Islamabad.
MOHSIN AKHTAR KAYANI J. Through the
instant petition, the petitioner has prayed for the
grant of post-arrest bail in criminal case F.I.R
No.40/23 dated 09.02.2023 registered under
Section 11 of PECA, 2016 read with Sections
295-A, 295-B, 295-C, 298-A, 109 PPC at P.S.
FIA, Cybercrime Circle, Islamabad.
2. Brief facts referred in the instant FIR
lodged on the complaint of Respondent No. 2,
Aamir Zafar, are as follows:-
“Consequent upon conclusion of enquiry No.
RE-171/2023 of FIA Cyber Crime Reporting
Center, Islamabad, it transpired that the
accused Raja Muhammad Adil s/o Raja
Muhammad Banaras r/o Pind Malhu. Tehsil
and District Rawalpindi. CNIC 42501-
7586051-5. User of Facebook Profile having
URL https://www.facebook.com/
profile.php?id=100085713667317 Profile
name: 'Salman Ahmad with criminal
intentions & ulterior motives, illegally and
unauthorizedly, created / developed and
further uploaded/transmitted/
2
Crl. Misc. No.1468-B-2025
disseminated as well as publicly projected /
displayed blasphemous contents i.e.,
Images / Pictures, in respect of The
Almighty The Holy Prophet
and
The Holy The Holy ﯽﻠﺻ
along with sacrilegious, loathsome
narration/speech, and text on private parts
of the necked human body using Facebook
Profile having URL
https://www.facebook.com/
profile.php?id=10008-5713667317 Profile
name: 'Salman Ahmad participating
with/in different Facebook Profile/s and /
Group/s and willfully defiled and outraged
Religious Feelings. Belief as well as Spirit
of Islam. Furthermore, during the course of
enquiry in the subject case, Mobile Phone
Set Huawei IMEI 1: 869783043770347 and
IMEI 2: 869783043810358, along with
mobile phone sims 0332-2120487, 0317-
5117176 as well as Facebook Profile
having URL:
https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=1
000857- 13667317 Profile name: 'Salman
Ahmad being used in the commission of
subject offences, were recovered from the
aforementioned accused Raja Muhammad
Adil.”
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner contends
that the petitioner is innocent and has falsely
been implicated in this case. He further submits
that his earlier post-arrest bail application, both
on merits as well as on statutory delay, was
dismissed by this Court through Crl.
Misc.No.817 of 2025 dated 09.05.2025. He also
submits that prior to the said dismissal, his first
post-arrest bail application on merits was
dismissed through Crl.Misc.No.631-B of 2023
dated 22.05.2023. Therefore, this is his third
post-arrest bail application, pressed on the
3
Crl. Misc. No.1468-B-2025
ground of statutory delay and non-compliance of
directions earlier granted by this Court.
4. Conversely, learned counsel for the
complainant as well as the State through learned
A.A.G. and the Investigating Officer of FIA, who
is in attendance, have opposed the instant post-
arrest bail application on the ground that delay
in the trial has been occasioned due to the
conduct of the petitioner, who has failed to
cross-examine the prosecution witnesses already
recorded. It is further contended that the ground
of statutory delay has already been dealt with by
this Court while dismissing the second post-
arrest bail application (Crl.Misc. No. 817 of 2025
dated 09.05.2025). Hence, a successive
application on a ground already settled by this
Court is not legally maintainable.
5. Arguments heard. Record perused.
6. Tentative assessment of the record reflects
that petitioner has been nominated in the
instant FIR with the allegation that he, with
ulterior motives, illegally created/developed
blasphemous content and images of the Almighty
تانئاک قلاخ ﷲ, the Holy Prophet ﷺ ﷴ ترضح نييبنلا متاخ,
Ahl al-Bayt نيعمجأ مهنع ىلاعت ﷲ ىضر, the Qur’an ديجم,
the Holy Mothers of the Believers ( ىضر نينمؤملا تاهما
اﮩنع ىلاعت ﷲ), along with sacrilegious remarks, and
4
Crl. Misc. No.1468-B-2025
uploaded the same in order to insult the
religious feelings of Muslims. The petitioner was
apprehended by the FIA authorities on
09.02.2023. The challan was submitted on
29.05.2023, and on the basis of the forensic
technical report, charge was framed on
05.09.2023. Three prosecution witnesses have
been recorded, out of which two have been cross-
examined at this stage.
7. The record further reflects that the
petitioner’s first post-arrest bail application on
merits was dismissed on 22.05.2023 in Criminal
Miscellaneous No.631-B of 2023, whereby this
Court directed the learned trial Court seized with
the matter to conclude the trial within a period
of eight months. However, the trial has not been
concluded, primarily due to the delay caused by
the petitioner’s side for not cross-examining the
prosecution witnesses, leading to repeated
adjournments at the request of the petitioner.
8. Thereafter, the petitioner again approached
this Court through Criminal Miscellaneous No.
817 of 2025, which was dismissed on
09.05.2025, including but not limited to the
ground of statutory delay. While rejecting the
said bail petition, this Court directed the learned
trial Court to conclude the trial within the next
5
Crl. Misc. No.1468-B-2025
two months by all means under intimation to
this Court. In case prosecution witnesses are not
cross-examined by the counsel for petitioner-
accused, the Court shall appoint counsel at State
expense to represent the accused for conclusion of
the trial positively.
9. Despite the said directions, the petitioner
has once again filed the instant application,
again invoking the ground of statutory delay as
well as non-compliance of the Court’s earlier
directions.
10. In view of the above scenario, and with the
able assistance of learned counsel for the parties
and the Law Officer, I have gone through the
order-sheet of the trial Court subsequent to the
dismissal of the second post-arrest bail
application, which reflects that case was fixed
before the trial Court on multiple occasions. A
tentative assessment of record reflects that
during the last four months, about 18 hearings
took place. The detail of the order-sheets is as
under:
Sr.
Date Court Proceedings / Remarks
No.
No prosecution witnesses in
1 16.05.2025

Learned counsel for the complainant
3 16.06.2025
has requested for adjournment.

11. The above order-sheets demonstrate that in
18 dates of hearing, at least 15 adjournments
were occasioned either due to absence of
7
Crl. Misc. No.1468-B-2025
prosecution witnesses, absence of record or case
property, or other lapses attributable to the
prosecution. Reliance is placed upon PLD 2023
SC 648 (Syeda A. Subhani Vs. The State &
others), wherein the august Supreme Court has
explained statutory period mentioned in the
third proviso of Section 497(1) Cr.P.C., namely
“that the trial of an accused must be
conducted expeditiously and that pre-
conviction detention of an accused person, in
offences not punishable with death, should
not extend beyond one year. If the trial is not
concluded within one year through no fault
of the accused, then a statutory right to bail
accrues in his favour unless his case falls
within the clauses of the fourth proviso”.
12. The august Court in 2024 SCMR 28
(Muhammad Usman Vs. The State and another)
further lays down that if the accused, after
rejection of bail on the ground of delay, corrects
himself and abstains from acts of delaying the
trial, but the prosecution still fails to perform its
duty in concluding the trial, a fresh right to bail
arises in his favour. The third proviso to Section
497(1) of Cr.P.C. would become operative, when
the period specific therein has expired before the
conclusion of trial without the fault of accused.
8
Crl. Misc. No.1468-B-2025
13. In the present case, earlier directions of
this Court to conclude the trial within two
months were not complied with. Out of 18
hearing dates, 15 adjournments were occasioned
due to the non-production of case property,
record, or prosecution witnesses. This delay is
attributable to the prosecution, and no
justifiable explanation has been offered.
Meanwhile, the accused has remained
incarcerated for over two years, whereas there
are only seven prosecution witnesses, three of
whom have already been examined with efforts of
the defence side.
14. The instant matter falls under the third
proviso of Section 497(1) Cr.P.C, where the
statutory period for offences punishable with
death is two years, and when this period of two
years is passed, the necessary condition is met.
Similar point has also been discussed in 2022
SCMR 1 (Shakeel Shah Vs. The State),
whereby the Hon’ble Supreme Court of Pakistan
has observed that for offences punishable with
death, the maximum permissible period of pre-
conviction detention is two years, beyond which
bail should be granted if the trial is not
concluded. In the present case, the petitioner
was apprehended on 09.02.2023, and more than
9
Crl. Misc. No.1468-B-2025
two years and seven months of pre-conviction
detention have elapsed. It is settled law that once
a direction is issued by this Court and the same
is not complied with by the trial Court or the
prosecution, and delay is attributable to the
prosecution, bail must follow.
15. For what has been discussed above, instant
petition is ALLOWED and the petitioner is
admitted to post arrest bail subject to his
furnishing bail bonds in the sum of
Rs.200,000/- with two sureties in the like
amount to the satisfaction of learned Trial Court.
(MOHSIN AKHTAR KAYANI)
JUDGE
RAMZAN

JUDGMENT SHEET
ISLAMABAD HIGH COURT, ISLAMABAD
JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT
Writ Petition No. 3566 of 2024
Sadeeq Anjam
Versus
The State and others
Petitioner by: Mr. Ali Azim Afridi, Advocate.
Respondents No.1 to 4 by: Mr. Fahad Khan Tareen,
Assistant Attorney General.
Sheikh Amir Sohail Anjum,
AD (Legal) and Muhammad
Haris Jabbar, AD (Inv),
NCCIA.
Respondent No.5 by: M/s Shah Khawar and Babar
Hayat Samor, Advocates.
Date of Hearing: 19.09.2025
INAAM AMEEN MINHAS, J:- The petitioner has invoked constitutional
jurisdiction of this Court under Article 199 of the Constitution of Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, 1973 read with section 561-A, Cr.P.C for quashing
FIR No.220 dated 11.09.2024, u/s 20 & 24 of the Prevention of Electronic
Crimes Act, 2016 (“PECA”) read with sections 505, 506(ii), 34 and 109 of
the Pakistan Penal Code,1860 (“PPC”), registered at police station Federal
Investigation Agency Cyber Crime Reporting Centre, Islamabad.
2. As per contents of the FIR, the allegation against the petitioner is that
he along with co-accused initiated a malicious campaign on different social
media platforms i.e. facebook, youtube and X (formerly twitter) to harass
blackmail defame respondent No.5/complainant along with his family as
well as built an ill-will narrative in the public through social media against
the entire judicial institution by declaring respondent No.5’s uncle as corrupt
upon baseless allegations without any proof.
2 W.P No.3566 of 2024
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the allegations
against the petitioner are baseless; that the instant FIR was registered against
the petitioner because of lodging of FIR and carrying legal proceedings
against the family members of respondent No.5 by him; that information
ending up in shape of registration of FIR No.2 of 2024 of Anti-Corruption
Police Station Bannu, shared by any or social application cannot be made
basis for registration of this FIR and that right to free speech is a
fundamental right.
4. The learned Assistant Attorney General as well as the learned counsel
for respondent No.5 opposed the instant writ petition and argued that the
allegations levelled against the petitioner are duly supported by the material
collected during the inquiry by FIA and that challan has been submitted
before the learned Trial Court, therefore, this Court should not interfere as
interference by this Court would amount to encroach upon the domain of the
learned Trial Court.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6. Perusal of the record reveals that respondent No.5 had submitted an
application before the FIA against the petitioner and the co-accused. The
FIA, after conducting an inquiry and collecting material, found sufficient
grounds and thereafter registered the FIR.
7. The petitioner has filed the instant petition to quash the FIR only to
his extent, whereas there are other seven co-accused. Partial quashing of an
FIR to the extent of some accused is a legal impossibility. Reliance is placed
upon Director General, Anti-Corruption Establishment, Lahore and others
vs. Muhammad Kamran Khan and others, (PLD 2013 SC 401).
8. Challan has been submitted before the learned Trial Court, where the
petitioner can avail alternate remedy available to him u/s 265-K, Cr.P.C. In
the case Supra, the Honourable Supreme Court also held that the law is quite
settled by now that after taking of cognizance of a case by a Trial Court, the
F.I.R. registered in that case cannot be quashed and the fate of the case and
of the accused persons challaned therein is to be determined by the Trial
3 W.P No.3566 of 2024
Court itself. It goes without saying that if after taking of cognizance of a
case by the Trial Court an accused person deems himself to be innocent and
falsely implicated and he wishes to avoid the rigorous of a trial then the law
has provided him a remedy under sections 249-A/265-K, Cr.P.C to seek his
premature acquittal, if the charge against him is groundless or there is no
probability of his conviction.
9. In view of the foregoing, the instant writ petition bears no merits,
therefore, the same stands dismissed.
(INAAM AMEEN MINHAS)
JUDGE
Announced in open Court on 26.09.2025.
JUDGE
R.Anjam

JUDGMENT SHEET.
ISLAMABAD HIGH COURT, ISLAMABAD
JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT.
Criminal Miscellaneous No.1239 of 2025
JIANPING XIAO AND OTHERS
Vs.
THE STATE AND ANOTHER
Petitioner by: M/s Sher Afzal Khan Marwat,
Ch. Usama Tariq and Haider
Khan, Advocates.
Respondents by: Mian Muhammad Irfan, Deputy
Attorney General. Ms. Mehak
Gull, Assistant Director/I.O,
NCCIA.
Date of Decision: 2.09.2025.
INAAM AMEEN MINHAS, J:- Through the instant Criminal
Miscellaneous Petition under section 561-A Cr.P.C, the petitioners have
assailed the order dated 04.07.2025 (“Impugned Order-I”), passed by
the learned Judicial Magistrate Section 30, Islamabad-West (“Trial
Court”) and order dated 08.07.2025 (“Impugned Order-II”), passed
by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Islamabad (West) (“Revisional
Court”), whereby application of the petitioner for superdari of mobile
phones and laptop was dismissed concurrently.
2. Brief facts are that the petitioners were arrested in case FIR
No.180/25, dated 27.06.2025, under sections 3, 4, 13, 14 & 16, PECA
Act, 2016 read with sections 419, 420, 109 & 34, PPC, registered at P.S
NCCIA, Cyber Crime Reporting Centre, Islamabad and at the time of
their arrest their personal belongings including laptops, eleven mobile
phones, gold rings, bracelets, lockets and cash amount of Rs.2.3 million
were taken into custody. The petitioners filed an application of
superdari of the articles, which was partially accepted by the learned
Trial Court vide the Impugned Order-I to the extent of one ring, one
2
Crl. Misc.No.1239/2025.
silver chain and one locket, whereas to the extent of remaining articles,
the application was dismissed. Feeling aggrieved, the petitioners filed a
criminal revision before the learned Revisional Court, which was
dismissed vide the Impugned Order-II, hence, this petition.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioners contended that the
personal belongings of the petitioners are not related to the commission
of any offence and hence their seizure is unlawful and without
justification and that mobile phones are essential tools of
communication and livelihood.
4. On the other hand, the learned Deputy Attorney General fully
supported the impugned orders and prayed for dismissal of the instant
petition.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the
record.
6. Perusal of the record reveals that the petitioners were arrested in
FIR No.180/25, dated 27.06.2025, under sections 3, 4, 13, 14 & 16
PECA, 2016 read with sections 419, 420, 109 & 34, PPC, registered at
P.S NCCIA, Cyber Crime Reporting Centre, Islamabad and during the
course of investigation 12 mobile phones, 4 laptops, 6 CPUs along with
other articles were taken into custody by the Investigation Officer.
Some items i.e. one ring, one silver chain and one locket were returned
to the petitioners on acceptance of the superdari by the learned Trial
Court. 12 mobile phones, 4 laptops and 6 CPUs have been sent to the
forensic laboratory for analysis and report, which are the case property
and their safe custody is necessary to unearth the digital trail, recover
incriminating material and corroborate the allegations. The recovered
mobile phones and laptops are not ordinary articles but are the tools
through which the offences under PECA and PPC are to be proved.
Any interruption or premature release of such devices risks alteration,
deletion or tampering with the data, which would render the forensic
examination meaningless.
3
Crl. Misc.No.1239/2025.
7. In view of the above discussion, the Impugned Order-I and
Impugned Order-II have been passed in accordance with law and do not
suffer from any illegality. The instant petition bears no merits,
therefore, the same stands dismissed.
(INAAM AMEEN MINHAS)
JUDGE
R.Anjam

2.
Precisely, the subject FIR stood registered against the petitioner on the

the petitioner in connivance with other accused persons persuaded the

and also filed the instant writ petition.
3. l,earned counsel contended that the petitioner has been implicated

5. Heard. The petitioner prays for quashingof FIR by invoking jurisdiction
vested in this Court in terms of Article 199 of the Constitution and in terms of
Section 561-A Cr.P.C. For and to exercise the jurisdiction in terms of Section
561-A Cr.P.C, the Hon'lole Apex Court in the recent pronouncement in the
case of "FIA th FIA and others v.
and others" (PLD 2023 SC 265) has graciously held that -
4. First of all, we want to make it clear that a High Court has no power
under Section 561-A CrPC to quash an FIR or an investigation
proceeding; therefore, the criminal miscellaneous applications filed
under Section 561-4, Cr.P.C by some of the accused persons in the
High Court for quashing the FIR and investigation proceeding in the
present case were not maintainable. This is because jurisdiction of a
High Court to make an appropriate order under Section 561-A Cr.P.C
necessary to secure the ends of justice, can only be exercised with
regard to the judicial or court proceedings and not relating to
proceedings of any other authority or department, such as FIR
registration or investigation proceedings of the police department. This
has been authoritatively held by a five-member bench of this Court in
Shahnaz Begum. A High Court, therefore, can quash a judicial
proceeding pending before any subordinate court under Section 561-A
CrPC, if it finds it necessary to make such order to prevent the abuse of
the process of that court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice;
however, it should not ordinarily exercise its power under Section 561-
A Cr.P.C to make such order unless the accused person has first avalled
his remedy before the trial court under Section 249-A or 265-K Cr.P.C.
6. As laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of F.I.A thtough

8. The petitioner in the present case intends to seek quashing of the FIR,
inter alia, on the grounds that he was falsely implicated by the FIA authorities
on account of professional jealousy at the behest of his opponents; that no
